item.title: Knicks fan’s ’go get Jesus’ jibe at LeBron James and 76ers backfires after 0-1 start
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images LeBron James helped the Philadelphia 76ers beat the New York Knicks 106-100 on the opening night of the new NBA season. Ahead of opening nights every year, we have seen bold declarations from almost every fan base, and some of them go a bit overboard. The Knicks were crowned champions last season, so their supporters had every reason to be optimistic. But one fan will probably regret what he said before the game. Knicks fan’s dig at LeBron James and the 76ers backfires Every fan is entitled to be optimistic about their side before the first whistle of the season, but one Knicks fan perhaps went a bit overboard. After a fantastic season last time out, this New York fan felt his side were above everyone else and would walk the NBA this season. He went as far as saying that even Jesus wouldn’t be able to save the 76ers, let alone new arrivals LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. The fan said on CNN: “On the trip last year, the NBA has been scrambling. So many people got traded to other teams. That’s what we do. We messed the NBA up so bad that everybody got switched over. “Not alone, the 76ers: They went and got LeBron, they went and got Brown. Who else do you want? Go get Jesus! He ain’t gonna save you. Still Knicks in five!” Unfortunately for the Knicks fan, his words backfired after the visitors ruined ring night at Madison Square Garden by beating the New Yorkers 106-100. The Knicks will want to return to winning ways after their opening night defeat when they take on the Boston Celtics, who have also lost their opening game.

item.title: Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool want to sign African superstar
item.description: Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool want to sign African superstar Fabrizio Romano has confirmed it, Liverpool now want to sign an African superstar. It's a fascinating time to be a supporter of the Reds right now. Everything is changing. From the ownership level where 1892 Holdings have acquired a significant minority stake in the club to the coaching staff. Andoni Iraola has heralded a new era with his arrival. Julian Ward is working above him as a sporting director. And then there's this new look squad. Liverpool's old core are long gone. Mo Salah and Andy Robertson who were the last few remnants of it, departed over the course of the summer. Virgil van Dijk and Alisson will depart soon, too. Their contracts expire at the end of the season. Instead, there are young players, and future superstars hoping to prove themselves. The next steps for Julian Ward as Liverpool sporting director Ward doesn't have an easy task at Liverpool. He's got a lot of work to do in terms of fixing the squad he inherited from Richard Hughes. The next steps for Ward will be to find balance in the team. Hughes brought in a lot of exciting young players. Some of those players could become the best in the world in their position one day. But Ward and Iraola now need to figure out the best way to put this team together and what's missing in the team as well. There are naturally obvious gaps in the squad. It's why Liverpool are not performing as well as some will have expected them to. Over time though, Iraola has shown he has the potential and the know-how to make this work. He could easily become the perfect successor to Jurgen Klopp's throne. Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool want Lamine Camara Undoubtedly, the biggest priority for the Reds will be to sign a midfielder. And not just any kind of midfielder but someone who is capable of holding their position and being a bit more defensive minded. Liverpool are missing a profile that is similar to what Fabinho brought to the team. One player who has been heavily linked is Lamine Camara. The former African Young Player of the Year, plays for the same team Fabinho joined Liverpool from AS Monaco. He is very defensive minded and he is also composed on the ball. And now Fabrizio Romano himself has confirmed Liverpool's interest. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he revealed Liverpool have been following Camara for a long time. “So, Liverpool are following Lamine Camara. They have been tracking him for a long time. There have been some calls regarding Alex Scott, and Liverpool have also been tracking Lamine Camara."

item.title: Maccabi Tel Aviv basketball rolls to 116-89 victory as Hapoel Jerusalem, Tel Aviv secure wins
item.description: HAPOEL JERUSALEM forward David Roddy drives to the basket for two of his game-high 16 points in the Reds Maccabi Tel Aviv cruised past Kiryat Ata 116-89 behind John DiBartolomeo's seven threes, while Hapoel Jerusalem, Hapoel Tel Aviv,, and Bnei Herzliya secured wins. Maccabi Tel Aviv cruised past Kiryat Ata 116-89 as captain John DiBartolomeo drained a career-high seven three-pointers to lead the yellow-and-blue to a convincing Israeli Premier League win. Oded Katash’s team established control early, with DiBartolomeo knocking down three triples in the opening stages. TJ Leaf, Armando Bacot and Bonzie Colson also found their rhythm, while Shane Hunter made his debut and finished in double figures. DiBartolomeo scored 21 points, Leaf added 17, and Bacot contributed 16. Holland Woods led Kiryat Ata with 18 points. “I’m happy that we won,” Katash said. “We pretty much had the game decided by the end of the first half, which allowed us to split up the minutes. We came into the game without some of our guards, which concerned me, but we didn’t really have an issue.” DiBartolomeo was pleased with his team’s approach following a demanding Euroleague double week. “We had good energy and focus,” he said. “It’s not easy after a tough double week, but we were happy that we could come in and begin the game well, which isn’t something to take for granted.” A flare in the Hapoel Jerusalem fans' stand. (credit: Liron Moldovan) Maccabi will next face Real Madrid in Euroleague action on Thursday. Hapoel Jerusalem defeats Beersheba with strong second-half performance In the capital, Hapoel Jerusalem defeated Hapoel Beersheba 88-74 after breaking away late in the first half and extending its advantage after the break. The teams were tied 30-30 before Kenny Lofton Jr., Eitan Burg and Lorenzo Brown helped the Reds take a 42-34 halftime lead. Brown then sparked a 9-0 run to open the third quarter, giving Jerusalem the separation it needed. David Roddy led Jerusalem with 16 points, while Lofton, Brown and Shake Milton scored 11 apiece. MJ Walker, Christian Coleman and Noam Avivi each finished with 11 points for Beersheba. Jerusalem coach Sasa Obradovic was unhappy with his team’s first-half performance despite the win. “We came in sloppy and not focused,” he said. “Even if the team we played didn’t have big-name guys, we have to be serious. The second half we were better, but we had to take this game better.” The Reds will next face Rigas Zelli in a EuroCup matchup. Hapoel Tel Aviv also won, overcoming Maccabi Ashdod 81-67 at the Drive In Arena behind Eugene German’s 31 points. Ashdod led 48-46 at halftime, with Robert Turner scoring 20 points, but Hapoel tightened its defense after the break, limiting the visitors to just 19 second-half points. Tomer Ginat added 12 points, while Antonio Blakeney scored 10. The second half we were better, but we had to take this game better.” The Reds will next face Rigas Zelli in a EuroCup matchup. Hapoel Tel Aviv also won, overcoming Maccabi Ashdod 81-67 at the Drive In Arena behind Eugene German’s 31 points. Ashdod led 48-46 at halftime, with Robert Turner scoring 20 points, but Hapoel tightened its defense after the break, limiting the visitors to just 19 second-half points. Tomer Ginat added 12 points, while Antonio Blakeney scored 10. Coach Dimitrios Itoudis said his team needed a halftime reset after an undisciplined opening performance. “You cannot come here, put on the Hapoel jersey, and play without an effort,” he said. Hapoel will now turn its attention to Bologna in the Euroleague. Bnei Herzliya outlasts Ness Ziona in double-overtime thriller Bnei Herzliya survived a double-overtime thriller to beat Ness Ziona 103-96. Zack Bryant led the winners with 23 points, DJ Brewton scored 21, and Dusty Hannahs added 20. Ness Ziona’s Josh Christopher poured in 30 points, while Jackson Rowe contributed 21. Herzliya coach Yehu Orland now hopes to carry the momentum into Wednesday’s Basketball Champions League clash against Porto, with advancement to the next round in Europe among the club’s goals. Hapoel HaEmek routed Maccabi Rishon Lezion 80-60 on the road to even its record at 1-1, despite entering the game following the dismissal of head coach Sharon Avraham over professional disagreements with management. Assistant Golan Jablonowsky took over on an interim basis. After trailing 33-30 at halftime, HaEmek dominated the second half, outscoring Rishon 50-27. Malik Hall led the visitors with 30 points, while Niv Misgav added 12. Justin Tillman scored 20 for Rishon, which fell to 0-2. Jablonowsky credited Avraham for his contribution to the team and said HaEmek’s return to its game plan after halftime proved decisive. Hapoel Eilat defeats Holon to maintain undefeated start Meanwhile, Hapoel Eilat defeated Hapoel Holon 78-69 at Begin Arena to improve to 2-0, leaving Holon winless after two games. James Dickey led Eilat with 21 points, while Kendale McCullum added 11. Rivaldo Soares scored 15 points for Holon and Shahar Amir contributed 12. Holon struggled from the three-point line, making just 10-of-33 attempts, while both teams committed 19 turnovers. In the north, Hapoel Galil Elyon edged Maccabi Ramat Gan 104-101 in a dramatic contest at Kfar Blum, leaving both teams with 1-1 records. Galil Elyon outscored Ramat Gan 33-23 in the third quarter to seize control and built a 16-point fourth-quarter lead. Ramat Gan mounted a late comeback and had a chance to cut the deficit to three, but a costly turnover let the hosts escape with the win. See more Israeli sports coverage at www.sportsrabbi.com/en

item.title: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama’s brutal shooting stat vs. Thunder is too wild to believe
item.description: Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Spurs star Victor Wembanyama’s brutal shooting stat vs. Thunder is too wild to believe appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming off a season in which the San Antonio Spurs won eight of their 12 contests (regular season and playoffs combined) against the Oklahoma City Thunder, Victor Wembanyama must have been brimming with confidence heading into the two sides’ clash on opening night. However, it’s hard to imagine the 7-foot-4 star having a worse shooting display than the one he had to begin the 2026-27 season. Wembanyama had 12 points on the night, and he had his moments defensively as well, recording six blocks against the Thunder. But of those 12 points, 10 came from the free-throw line. The Spurs star made just one of his 13 field-goal attempts on the night, missing all four of his shots from beyond the arc. The only field goal Wembanyama made came in the dying seconds of the third quarter, when he punched home an alley-oop from De’Aaron Fox. This is quite the outlier performance from Wembanyama; he did not have a single game last season with fewer than three made field-goals. In five regular-season games against the Thunder last season, he averaged 18.4 points and shot 52.4% from the field. In the seven-game Western Conference Finals series, he averaged 27.3 points on 48.1% shooting. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This is also a complete 180 of his season-opening performance last season , when he recorded 40 points on 15-of-21 shooting in a 33-point blowout of the Dallas Mavericks. The Thunder defense deserve a lot of credit for flustering Wembanyama. Isaiah Hartenstein was bruising him up yet again, while Chet Holmgren didn’t completely wilt against the man who considers him as his archnemesis. Aday Mara also had his moments against the Spurs star. But the touch simply wasn’t there for Wembanyama on the night, and towards the end of the game, it looked as though his confidence in his jumpshot had vanished completely. Nonetheless, this is only one game, and there are no reasons for Spurs fans to hit the panic button. Related: Spurs’ Stephon Castle opens up on ‘hardest part’ of defending Sha Gilgeous-Alexander Related: Thunder HC Mark Daigneault speaks up on defense that Victor Wembanyama couldn’t solve

item.title: Teen racing driver makes history in car built with dad
item.description: Dara McInerney has been competing in the BRSCC Junior Fiesta Championship for just two seasons. [BBC] A teenage racing driver who helped build his own championship-winning car with his father has broken records in junior motorsport. Dara McInerney, who is from Mow Cop in Staffordshire, has spent the past two seasons competing in the BRSCC Fiesta Junior Championship. This year, he finished on the podium in 17 of his 18 races, winning 14 of them - the most victories recorded in a single season, according to organisers. Looking back, the 16-year-old described his record-breaking achievements as "a bit surreal". "It's very impressive considering it's just me and my dad," he said. Dara McInerney in his first go-kart, aged three [Family Handout] His love of motorsport started long before he was old enough to race. "I was sat on his lap doing the steering while he was doing the pedals," Dara said, recalling his earliest memories of being in a car with his father, Craig. "It just sort of came naturally once he got me in a car. I was just gone the second I could touch both pedals." Now one of the championship's standout drivers, Dara said his first time driving on a circuit, at the age of 13, was "very daunting". "But now I don't feel that nervous; it just feels normal," he said. The pair spend much of their spare time preparing their Ford Fiesta for race weekends, with Dara taking on much of the engineering work. "I've built a few engines myself," he said. "I've built this car myself. Every nut and bolt has been off it." Dara, who is homeschooled, hopes to progress further in motorsport and one day compete in World GT racing. For now, his focus is on winning more races. The teenager recently completed his second season finishing his last two races at Oulton Park in pole position [Family Handout] Craig, who has a background in mechanical engineering, has helped Dara with his academic studies and taught him the practical skills needed to maintain and rebuild a racing car. "When we started building this car, he did most of the work and continues to do so," he said. "During the week, he rebuilds the car, strips it down and checks it." Craig said he was often reminded how unusual his son's abilities were for someone his age. "He's 16, and he does more than a lot of adults probably could do, and I'm very proud of that, never mind the driving," he said. Craig McInerney has passed on his mechanical engineering skills and knowledge of cars to his son [BBC] "He'll pick anything up and fix it, and it's not just engines and cars; it's electricals as well. Anything practical, he'll do." As Dara's success has grown, Craig said the family had started receiving praise from people across the motorsport world. He believes his son has the talent to achieve his ambition of racing in World GT if he can secure the backing needed to progress. item.title: Where to watch Wizards vs. Bucks today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener
item.description: Where to watch Wizards vs. Bucks today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Wizards will open up the regular season with a home matchup against the Bucks taking place Wednesday night. After a five-year playoff drought, Washington is looking to turn the page, and several offseason additions could make it possible this season. The Wizards snagged BYU's AJ Dybantsa as the No. 1 overall pick in the draft, though the rookie suffered an ankle sprain in a matchup against the Pelicans on Friday. Dybantsa is currently considered day-to-day. Meanwhile, the Bucks are trying to find their new identity after trading away long-time star Giannis Antetokounmpo. Milwaukee is certainly in a rebuilding phase, with new head coach Taylor Jenkins basically starting from scratch. Guard Tyler Herro has been a solid addition though, contributing 25 points in the team's preseason win over Indiana. Who will start the regular season off with a victory? Here's everything you need to know about Wizards vs. Bucks today, including TV channel and streaming options for the NBA season opener. Where to watch Wizards vs. Bucks today TV channels: Monumental Sports Network (Washington), MY24 (Milwaukee) Live streams: DAZN (Washington) The Wizards-Bucks game will be televised locally on Monumental Sports Network in Washington, and MY24 in Milwaukee. Those in the DC market can also watch live and on-demand with DAZN . DAZN is Washington's new direct-to-consumer media partner, set to air preseason and regular-season games along with additional Wizards content all season long ( read more here ). All games not selected for exclusive national broadcast by one of the league's partners will be available to stream live and on-demand with DAZN, which offers a free trial for new subscribers. item.title: Max Eberl pleased Sacha Boey got a chance in Bayern Munich’s win over RB Leipzig
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 17: Sacha Boey of FC Bayern Muenchen with the ball during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between FC Bayern München and RB Leipzig at Allianz Arena on October 17, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images In what was billed to be much more of a contest on the heels of two straight draws for Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga champions handily dispatched RB Leipzig, winning 6-1 at the Allianz Arena over the weekend. They now have exactly the momentum they were looking for ahead of a massive Champions League clash against Arsenal this week and were able to give some players a rest in the second half with the comfortable lead they held over Leipzig. Vincent Kompany used all five substitutions in the win over Leipzig, allowing Konrad Laimer, Harry Kane, Ismael Saibari, and Aleksandar Pavlović to get at least some rest in the second half. It is expected that most of those players will be back in his starting lineup for the Arsenal match. Min-jae Kim was also taken off in the second half, though it might not have been fully planned by Bayern. After the match, board member for sport Max Eberl—who covered media duties due to Kompany’s hip problem and recovery from an illness—explained that Kim was experiencing a few minor issues, which is why he was replaced by Sacha Boey in the 77th minute. For Boey, it was his first appearance of the season for Bayern after a summer where the club failed to find a proper destination for him during the transfer window. They had made it clear the player was not in Kompany’s plans for this season, but nothing wound up materializing for the Frenchman. As such, Eberl said he was happy Boey was able to make a cameo against L eipzig, noting that the defender has remained intensely professional despite a tough situation. “That was nice. Minjae was having a few problems, so he had to come off. Sacha gives 100% in training. He throws himself into everything. He knows that his situation here is extremely difficult. Bu t he got his chance today. The coach rewarded him for his performances in training, and that’s a great thing t o see,” Eberl stressed to B ild (via @iMiaSanMia ). Even though the club greatly appreciates how Boey has handled everything and how he continues to conduct himself professionally, there is still not a long-term future for him in the current setup. The January transfer window will provide another opportunity for a potential solution to be found for the defender. Join the conversation! item.title: Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls
item.description: Steve Tandy was defence coach on the British and Irish Lions tour to South Africa in 2021 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] After over a year and 13 games as Wales head coach, Steve Tandy is getting used to making tough phone calls and then copping flak when his selections are made public. Tandy named his 39-man squad for November's Nations Championship on Tuesday, with the 11am announcement prompting the usual tribal responses. There was delight at the inclusions of uncapped trio Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barratt and recalls for Rio Dyer, Seb Davies, Taine Basham and Gabriel Hamer-Webb. There was also disappointment at the omissions of Taulupe Faletau, Macs Page, Elliot Dee, Bryn Bradley, Mason Grady and Tommy Reffell, who Tandy later revealed had suffered a knee injury. "There'll be people out there challenging me on selections," said the head coach, who has now named four squads. "No-one really says who they would leave out either, it's always the people that should be in! It's something that comes with the territory." Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call Tandy left his role as Scotland's defence coach to call the shots for his country in the summer of 2025. He has used 54 players so far and is still casting his net wide despite it being just under a year until the World Cup gets under way. Tandy will be limited to 33 players for the tournament in Australia but has selected a squad of 39 for the Nations Championship. "I cop flak wherever I go, that's something I'm getting used to. I get some of that, but you can only pick so many," said the former Ospreys flanker and boss. "Martyn [Williams, team manager] would have kicked off if I had gone with more, he wouldn't be happy with the budget! "I'm comfortable in this space and know that we are thorough around our selection. "There have been some brilliant performances out there from boys that are not in. I've had some phone calls over the last few days that were tough, but I'd rather the boys know where they sit." Opportunity knocks in World Cup countdown Wales have just 12 or 13 games until they get their World Cup campaign under way against Zimbabwe. item.content:encoded: Steve Tandy was defence coach on the British and Irish Lions tour to South Africa in 2021 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] After over a year and 13 games as Wales head coach, Steve Tandy is getting used to making tough phone calls and then copping flak when his selections are made public. Tandy named his 39-man squad for November's Nations Championship on Tuesday, with the 11am announcement prompting the usual tribal responses. There was delight at the inclusions of uncapped trio Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barratt and recalls for Rio Dyer, Seb Davies, Taine Basham and Gabriel Hamer-Webb. There was also disappointment at the omissions of Taulupe Faletau, Macs Page, Elliot Dee, Bryn Bradley, Mason Grady and Tommy Reffell, who Tandy later revealed had suffered a knee injury. "There'll be people out there challenging me on selections," said the head coach, who has now named four squads. "No-one really says who they would leave out either, it's always the people that should be in! It's something that comes with the territory." Wales great Faletau still has drive for fourth World Cup Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call Tandy left his role as Scotland's defence coach to call the shots for his country in the summer of 2025. He has used 54 players so far and is still casting his net wide despite it being just under a year until the World Cup gets under way. Tandy will be limited to 33 players for the tournament in Australia but has selected a squad of 39 for the Nations Championship. "I cop flak wherever I go, that's something I'm getting used to. I get some of that, but you can only pick so many," said the former Ospreys flanker and boss. "Martyn [Williams, team manager] would have kicked off if I had gone with more, he wouldn't be happy with the budget! "I'm comfortable in this space and know that we are thorough around our selection. "There have been some brilliant performances out there from boys that are not in. I've had some phone calls over the last few days that were tough, but I'd rather the boys know where they sit." Wales counting down the year until World Cup Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup? Opportunity knocks in World Cup countdown Wales have just 12 or 13 games until they get their World Cup campaign under way against Zimbabwe. It would be understandable if Tandy was keen to whittle down his options, but he is still keen to reward performances. "I'd never give out an opportunity, they've got to earn it, and I think I am pretty clear on the core of our group," he said. "But this is another opportunity to see someone else in our environment and see what comes out of it." That is the case with the uncapped Dragons pair of centre Owen and scrum-half Hope, but the selection of their Rodney Parade team-mate Davies was more surprising. The lock or flanker, in his second season with Dragons after moving from Cardiff, has 17 caps, but has not featured since facing Italy in the 2022 Six Nations. Wales already have Dafydd Jenkins, Ben Carter, Adam Beard and Teddy Williams in their squad and are highly unlikely to take five second-row forwards to the World Cup, but Tandy is still keen to cast his eye over the 30-year-old. "You see the athletic ability with Seb and speaking to him there was the emotional outpouring of being involved with the squad," Tandy said. "We had an alignment camp – a smaller unit gathering – and he came in to get to know them. With that exposure, it's a great opportunity to see boys in our environment." Page waits for turn Macs Page made his 50th Scarlets appearance against Newcastle this month [Huw Evans Picture Agency] One in-form player who must wait for his opportunity is Page, who has caught the eye on the wing for Scarlets. The 21-year-old has scored four tries in four appearances, while he has made nine line breaks. He misses out with Dyer and Hamer-Webb coming in to join Josh Adams, Ellis Mee, Blair Murray, Tom Rogers and Louis Rees-Zammit. "Macs has been outstanding but that's where the depth of our wingers and back field is really encouraging," Tandy told Scrum V podcast. "Look at others - Mason Grady, Keelan Giles, Tom Bowen, all those boys are playing well. Jacob Beetham was outstanding at the start of the season [before injury]." Dyer was selected by Tandy last autumn and won his 24th cap against South Africa, but missed out on the Six Nations and summer Tests. The Dragons back has been a threat with ball in hand and, like Scarlets rival Mee, has thrived when chasing restarts and kicks. "Some of his aerial contests have been better than anyone in Wales," said Tandy. "Rio has really developed that and his work rate has been outstanding. He thoroughly deserves his recall." What is Wales' best centre partnership? Two of Eddie James' three starts for Scarlets this season have been at inside centre [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Tandy has fielded five different midfield partnerships so far, and could add to that tally after Owen's call-up. Ben Thomas started against South Africa in July but misses out because of a calf injury, with the uncapped Dragons centre now pushing for a chance at 12. Owen, a member of the Wales squad in the summer 2021 after a breakthrough season when he broke up the expected partnership of Jamie Roberts and Nick Tompkins, has been rewarded for club excellence. "He has been outstandingly consistent and does everything really well. Speak to coaches and they mention his standards on and off the field, how he is the last one off after working on extras," Tandy told Scrum V . "He has had injuries, and you could argue he could have been in the selection mix sooner, but what I love is that he has kept going and kept getting better. "He has been so consistent and at a high level, not just seven out of 10 but above that." Owen is a specialist 12 to rival Joe Hawkins, who is with Scarlets in South Africa to play Stormers this weekend along with Taine Plumtree. Eddie James is one of the five Wales squad members to stay at home, with Tandy likely to field him in the Nations Championship opener against Japan. There has been debate about the powerful back's best position - with many feeling he has the bulk for inside centre, where he started Scarlets' first two games of the season - but Tandy is sticking to his guns. "I see Eddie more as a 13. He can definitely play 12, as we have seen for the Scarlets, but in our team he is more of a 13 who can play 12," he said. "Louie Hennessey, Max Llewellyn and Eddie, they have big frames and there is lot of interchangeability for the 12s and 13s. We have a nice variety of options there." Tandy has made his first selection of the Nations Championship, but there is plenty more scrutiny ahead with four team announcements to come.

item.title: ‘It’s a lot’ – Jalen Hurts’ former teammate A.J. Brown sends heartfelt message to Eagles star
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Jalen Hurts’ former teammate A.J. Brown has addressed his medical situation, sharing a wholesome message for the Philadelphia superstar. Messages of support for Jalen Hurts have been pouring in from all over the NFL and the wider sports world ever since the full extent of his health issues was made public. The Eagles star is set to miss the entire season, and it could possibly seriously affect his entire career, too. One of Hurts’ most iconic former teammates has now reached out. A.J. Brown and Jalen Hurts spent four seasons together with the Philadelphia Eagles from 2022 to 2025. The duo helped the Eagles reach two Super Bowls and won a championship in 2024. A.J. Brown shares his love and respect for Jalen Hurts, saying he is ‘praying for him’ Brown left the Eagles under a cloud. He is now with the New England Patriots. Despite his great relationship with the QB, the star receiver was openly unhappy with his role on the team in 2025. It doesn’t seem to have affected how he views Hurts, though. Asked about the situation, A.J. shared his support for his ex-teammate, speaking straight from the heart. “Yeah, I’m getting the news just like you are. It’s a tough situation, man,” Brown said. “Got a lot of love and respect for him. Praying for him. You know how serious it was, all of us kind of found that out. But he’s a tough guy. He can handle anything. He can handle it. I pray that God continue to keep his hand on him. It’s a lot of love and respect for him this way. So, speedy recovery.” Teammates and rivals alike are all hoping to see Hurts bounce back from the situation he finds himself in. It is likely to be a long journey for the Eagles quarterback, but hopefully, the Super Bowl winner will be back on the field as soon as possible. item.title: Fabregas and Como prepare for historic Man Utd tie
item.description: The picturesque setting of Como's Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium, by the banks of Lake Como [Getty Images] "It's Manchester United. We are only just getting our heads around the fact we are playing Inter, Milan and Juventus. "This is without doubt the biggest night in the club's history." The words of a Como staff member say it all. United may not be the force they once were and travel to Italy on the brink of a full-blown crisis after six games without a win, their worst run since 2018-19. But, in terms of global stature, they are immense. To put this into context, when United savoured the last of their three Champions League triumphs in 2008, Como were a Serie D club, playing in one of nine semi-professional regional leagues, where attendances tend to be measured in their hundreds. According to chief executive Mirwan Surwaso, it was their status as an amateur club - they returned to Serie D in 2017 after being unable to convince the authorities of their financial wellbeing - which first attracted the London-based media company Sent Entertainment, owned by Indonesian billionaires Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono. When they concluded a deal in 2019, the Hartono brothers were planning a TV project, with the idea of screening matches involving young Indonesian players back home. A visit from Manchester United was not part of the plan. The Aero Club at the back of a stand at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium [Getty Images] There cannot be many Champions League stadiums you can walk around and in addition to seeing an iconic tourist attraction. Lake Como is 29 miles long and 2.5 miles wide in some parts - you also come across a yacht club and an 'Aero Club' for the sea-planes that take off at regular intervals. The clubs themselves have been there for a long time. But Como also use their natural surroundings to offer one hour Lake Como tours, followed by 'pre-match Lakeside hospitality'. In town - Como's population is just over 83,000, which means 90% of them could fit in the San Siro Stadium - there is a plush new club shop, selling all kinds of branded merchandise. There was no need for that in Serie D. "Somehow the team got promoted, we had to go professional, and the plan had to be scrapped," Surwaso told Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored Podcast this month. The alternative plan is still being amended substantially. Initially it was expected this season would be a selling year, when some of the developing talents Como thought they could cash in on would be sold. Instead, manager Cesc Fabregas steered his squad to fourth place in 2025-26, capitalising on AC Milan's shock defeat at Cagliari. It meant in the space of five seasons from Fabregas' arrival as a player, Como had gone from Serie B to the Champions League. Earlier this week, Lionel Messi's son Ciro gave Como his seal of approval by being pictured with his dad wearing a replica Como kit. Tangible evidence of a meteoric rise. Former France internationals Raphael Varane (left) and
item.content:encoded: The picturesque setting of Como's Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium, by the banks of Lake Como [Getty Images] "It's Manchester United. We are only just getting our heads around the fact we are playing Inter, Milan and Juventus. "This is without doubt the biggest night in the club's history." The words of a Como staff member say it all. United may not be the force they once were and travel to Italy on the brink of a full-blown crisis after six games without a win, their worst run since 2018-19. But, in terms of global stature, they are immense. To put this into context, when United savoured the last of their three Champions League triumphs in 2008, Como were a Serie D club, playing in one of nine semi-professional regional leagues, where attendances tend to be measured in their hundreds. According to chief executive Mirwan Surwaso, it was their status as an amateur club - they returned to Serie D in 2017 after being unable to convince the authorities of their financial wellbeing - which first attracted the London-based media company Sent Entertainment, owned by Indonesian billionaires Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono. When they concluded a deal in 2019, the Hartono brothers were planning a TV project, with the idea of screening matches involving young Indonesian players back home. A visit from Manchester United was not part of the plan. The Aero Club at the back of a stand at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium [Getty Images] There cannot be many Champions League stadiums you can walk around and in addition to seeing an iconic tourist attraction. Lake Como is 29 miles long and 2.5 miles wide in some parts - you also come across a yacht club and an 'Aero Club' for the sea-planes that take off at regular intervals. The clubs themselves have been there for a long time. But Como also use their natural surroundings to offer one hour Lake Como tours, followed by 'pre-match Lakeside hospitality'. In town - Como's population is just over 83,000, which means 90% of them could fit in the San Siro Stadium - there is a plush new club shop, selling all kinds of branded merchandise. There was no need for that in Serie D. "Somehow the team got promoted, we had to go professional, and the plan had to be scrapped," Surwaso told Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored Podcast this month. The alternative plan is still being amended substantially. Initially it was expected this season would be a selling year, when some of the developing talents Como thought they could cash in on would be sold. Instead, manager Cesc Fabregas steered his squad to fourth place in 2025-26, capitalising on AC Milan's shock defeat at Cagliari. It meant in the space of five seasons from Fabregas' arrival as a player, Como had gone from Serie B to the Champions League. Earlier this week, Lionel Messi's son Ciro gave Como his seal of approval by being pictured with his dad wearing a replica Como kit. Tangible evidence of a meteoric rise. Former France internationals Raphael Varane (left) and Thierry Henry (centre) are both investors in Como [Getty Images] Not night and day, another world - Fabregas Como head coach Cesc Fabregas with Argentine forward Nico Paz [Getty Images] "Compared to when I finished my career here, it is completely different," said Fabregas. "It is not even night and day. It is another world. "Playing Manchester United is a historic day once again for the club, the city of Como and fanbase. "When I retired as a player, I coached to get experience. I explained what I thought of the club and my vision and put the plan to work. We are a family here. Even when we lose, fans come and celebrate. We need to be humble and remember who we were because the story of Como will be beautiful, and we will remember it forever." The captivating nature of the Como story does bring with it some questions. In the short term, some wonder how they can possibly comply with Uefa's financial rules, which European football's governing body does not intend to amend despite Como's rise from Serie B. Surwaso told Morgan: "The scrutiny is on us but we always have our books in order, so we are not too worried." The other point, which will become an issue if the forecast heavy rain at kick-off arrives, is that three quarters of the 12,300-capacity Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is uncovered. Growing both sides of the club is essential if Como are to maximise their potential. For Fabregas, whose responsibility is clearly on the playing side, there is a balance to be struck between celebrating the spectacular journey Como have been on, and ensuring his players are not resting on their laurels. "We were at minus 10 when we started, but we don't want to spend time thinking about what has passed," said the former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea star. "If you want to do that, retire and go write a book about what Como did. We must look at what is in front of us." Como fans show their support before the club's Champions League debut against RB Leipzig on 10 September [Getty Images] While Como now attract thousands to their games, those who followed the club when crowds were in the hundreds remain. "I had an uncle who supported Como," said Marco Melillo, an out-of-town fan. "He showed me the sticker collection, I saw the blue shirt and the blue colours and totally went crazy about it. "I know in England a lot of people support teams in lower leagues, but that is not so true in Italy, where people support bigger teams. I do not like that that much. I was not really interested in supporting a team that was winning something. I liked the colours. I liked the stadium and when I came here and saw the lake, it was 'wow'. "We know the club is in the best situation ever in its history but when I see the faces of the guys and ladies that were also here in Serie D, we just see in our eyes and say, 'OK, we hope that this story will go on as long as possible, as best as possible, but if it maybe abruptly ended, because in the past we had also some bad things, we know we will be there'." Federico Borghi is a local, and despite the weather, came with his huge Como 1907-2007 history book. "In 2008, I had just started to go to the stadium to attend games," he said. "Not even in our best dreams could we think of playing Manchester United. I get chills even thinking about it. "As soon as I entered the stadium for the first time I realised this was going to be my faith. I was there in the bad times and that has strengthened my faith and my relationship with the club. "The Premier League is my inspiration and to face one of the top three or four biggest clubs in the world, it's a big honour." item.title: Man Utd make decision on selling injury-prone Red who’s awaiting first start in almost a year
item.description: Man Utd make decision on selling injury-prone Red who’s awaiting first start in almost a year Manchester United reportedly have no plans to part ways with Matthijs de Ligt during their defensive revamp, despite his 11-month-long injury layoff. The centre-half is in line to feature tonight for the first time since November 2025, after which he sustained a back problem that required surgery to correct. Matthijs de Ligt on verge of long-awaited return (Photo via ManUtd) It means Michael Carrick has had to navigate his entire reign with one fewer option at the back, so he’ll undoubtedly welcome having the experienced Red at his disposal in the coming weeks. De Ligt has been training this week in preparation for tonight’s clash with Como, though Carrick is navigating a depleted squad for matchday three of the Champions League. Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez were all absent from Tuesday’s open training session at Carrington, as well as Leny Yoro due to his suspension, which has prompted concerns from supporters over how the side may fare. De Ligt to stay put next summer (Photo via club media) Ahead of De Ligt making his return to action , MailSport has revealed that United are preparing for a future with him playing a key role. The 27-year-old is under contract until 2029, having signed a five-year deal when he signed from Bayern Munich in 2024, and the club have the option of extending his stay by an additional 12 months. Meanwhile, counterparts Martinez and Harry Maguire are out of contract at the end of the season, with only the former’s terms containing a one-year option. However, there is uncertainty over the Argentine’s future and whether INEOS will trigger the clause following his outburst in Madrid last week, which saw him express his disdain for the board’s lack of investment. There wasn’t much movement among the top quarterback prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft during a wild Week 7 in college football, but we did learn a lot about many of the top names in the class. No. 1 quarterback Drew Mestemaker continued to show off his incredible arm talent in a high-scoring loss to Houston on Saturday night, but it wasn’t all perfect. While the throws he did make were awe-inspiring as usual, some of his recklessness with the ball did show up, and it is going to cost the Cowboys in the Big 12 title race. Trinidad Chambliss played another great game from the pocket in a 31-3 win over Missouri, while Austin Simmons was under fire all day from the Ole Miss defense. C.J. Carr nearly led Notre Dame back from a late deficit in a loss to BYU, while Darian Mensah had to go back and forth against a talented Florida State defense in an epic double-overtime win. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ohio State’s Julian Sayin also dropped out of the top 10 this week, as a lot of his flaws showed up in an ugly win over Indiana. Sayin was rattled by the Hoosiers’ pressure, and as a result he was late to see a lot of what was happening downfield. When he’s even a tick off, his lack of arm strength amplifies the problem. Sayin also suffered an elbow injury that may keep him out for the rest of the season. Arguably the biggest draft-related storyline coming out of Week 7 is Arch Manning . Once again, Manning had his moments in a loss to Florida on Saturday, but his tape is still littered with misfires and mental mistakes that are costing the Longhorns games. There will be a floor that Manning will reach in his prospect profile because of his physical tools, but seeing him play like this week after week is concerning at best. How far did Manning fall, and where do the rest of the top quarterbacks stack up coming out of a wild Week 7? Let’s get into the list. 1. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Last week: 1 Mestemaker can make throws that nobody else in this draft class can, point blank. His throw moving to his left against Houston to set the Cowboys up in the red zone was truly special and is a perfect example of why he is the top QB prospect in this class at the moment. Drew Mestemaker oh my goodness He did the Zach Wilson Pro Day throw in a live game pic.twitter.com/JGzIe48e3r — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) October 18, 2026 Mestemaker isn’t a perfect prospect, which is to be expected for someone who has only been playing the position for a few years now. His ball security, both handling the ball in the pocket and decision making when throwing down the field. But he continues to grow and carry this Oklahoma State offense, and he stays as a rock-solid No. 1 as a result. 2. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss Last week: 2 Chambliss didn’t use his legs much on Saturday in a win over Missouri, but he didn’t have to. Week in and week out, Chambliss continues to showcase his development as a pocket passer. He is unafraid to push the ball down the field and attack between the hashes, and it unlocks the entire field for this Ole Miss offense. Now, Chambliss has his toughest test yet. While all the discussion about Texas has centered around the inconsistencies of Manning and the offense, the Longhorns’ defense has been one of the best in college football. Colin Simmons, a projected top-10 pick and the nation’s sack leader, isn’t expected to play in this game , but Chambliss still has his work cut out for him. 3. Darian Mensah, Miami (FL) Last week: 4 Mensah had been dinking and dunking for a lot of 2026 to this point, but it was bombs away in a 43-35 double-overtime win over Florida State. Mensah looked the way of Malachi Toney early and often in this game, and his out-of-structure playmaking was on display as well. Overall, the Duke transfer finished 23-of-34 with 326 yards and three touchdowns with an interception. 4. C.J. Carr, Notre Dame Rob Gray-Imagn Images Last week: 5 Carr wasn’t perfect on Saturday night against BYU, and his game will likely be remembered for his costly blunder on a failed spike at the end of the first half that cost the Irish points. But the second half was an admirable showing from Carr, who led the Irish down the field multiple times in obvious passing situations in a hostile environment against a very good defense. Carr isn’t going to wow you with his athleticism, but his ability to stand in the pocket and make throws makes him a clear first-round prospect. 5. Arch Manning, Texas Last week: 3 I’m not even sure where to start with Manning at this point. The talent is there, and it was again in the loss to Florida on Saturday when he made one of the plays and throws of the year to help chip into Florida’s late lead. But, as he did against Oklahoma, he dug Texas into that hole with careless turnovers, bad decisions and too many empty plays caused by his poor processing. It’s hard to parse the difference in the Steve Sarkisian offense over the last few years. Quinn Ewers had easy throw after easy throw all over the field, while Manning feels like he gets nothing open outside of the screen game. How much of that falls on Sark, and how much falls on Manning for not seeing the game clearly? 6. Austin Simmons, Missouri Last week: 6 Simmons’ tape didn’t look nearly as bad as the 31-3 score on Saturday, but it was still a struggle for he and this Missouri offense against Pete Golding and the Rebels. The Ole Miss transfer is still a pure pocket passer, and while you would like to see him use his athleticism a little bit more at times, there aren’t many in this class with the level of arm that Simmons has. 7. LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Last week: 8 Sellers didn’t play in Week 7, but the signs he continues to show as a passer and a processor from the pocket are very encouraging when you pair them with what he is as an athlete. If Sellers continues to build on this, which isn’t a given considering his history, he could continue to rise up these rankings. Things will get a little bit tougher for Sellers and the South Carolina offense on Saturday when they take on a Tennessee defense that completely shut down both Texas and Alabama in recent weeks. 8. Dante Moore, Oregon Last week: 7 Moore still hasn’t played since his concussion, and it’s unclear when he might return to the field for an Oregon team that desperately needs him. The Ducks have very slim playoff hopes that they are still clinging to, but they need Moore back out there in order to reach them. 9. Jayden Maiava, USC Last week: 10 Maiava and USC also had the week off in Week 7, but they continue to hang around in the CFP race on the back of a quietly excellent season from the senior quarterback. If Maiava wants to move up this list, he will have to prove it over the next few games. USC goes on the road to Madison to take on a much-improved Wisconsin team on Saturday before a game against Ohio State on Halloween. 10. Drake Lindsey, Minnesota Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Last week: NR Lindsey has one of the best arms in this draft class, and he continues to win games at Minnesota despite not having a whole lot of help around him on offense. His ceiling remains unclear due to limited athleticism, but Lindsey’s pro-style background and his great physical traits will make him a high floor pick in the mid-to-late rounds this spring. Next five: Julian Sayin (Ohio State), CJ Bailey (NC State), Brendan Sorsby, Nico Iamaleava (UCLA), Sam Leavitt (LSU) Related: Georgia HC Kirby Smart reveals Gunner Stockton actually has shoulder injury, not concussion Related: Urban Meyer backs Jon Sumrall as coach to bring Florida back to college football summit

item.title: ‘Ain’t no way’ – Patrick Mahomes’ ex-teammate makes massive 76ers prediction after defeating Knicks
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes’ ex-teammate LeSean McCoy reiterated his lifelong Philadelphia 76ers fandom after watching the team pick up a 106-100 win over the New York Knicks. The 76ers have got their 2026-27 season campaign off to a winning start by defeating the defending champions and establishing their credentials as contenders after a major offseason reshuffle. While many have the 76ers pegged as favourites after the additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, McCoy has gone a step further with a bold prediction after watching the first win of the season. 76ers win has LeSean McCoy dreaming of the NBA Finals McCoy was tuned into the 76ers vs. Knicks clash on opening night, watching his 76ers have success over the Knicks and then predicting them to make it to the 2026 NBA Finals . “Ain’t no way you can stop us… SIXERS BOUND (FOR) FINALS.” This was an impressive performance by the 76ers, led by Tyrese Maxey’s 28 points on 9-for-19 shooting, with new addition Jaylen Brown contributing 19 points, eight rebounds, and six assists. LeBron James scored 14 points with nine rebounds and seven assists in his debut with the franchise. The Knicks’ offence came to a sputtering halt in front of a spirited 76ers defensive performance, with Jalen Brunson’s 21 points on 6-for-19 the best scoring performance. Karl-Anthony Towns had a solid night with 19 points and 12 rebounds, but seemed underutilised with a 6-for-9 shooting performance. McCoy is a Philadelphia-area legend and is the all-time rushing yards leader for the NFL’s Philadelphia Eagles. He’s a Philadelphia native who was drafted by his hometown NFL team, and roots for the 76ers with just as fierce a passion. McCoy and Mahomes were teammates for the Kansas City Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIV win in 2019, and then played opposite Mahomes in Super Bowl LV, winning it with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Mahomes’ expense. item.title: Beitar, Maccabi Tel Aviv soccer battle to scoreless draw as Hapoel Tel Aviv defies early red card
item.description: BEITAR JERUSALEM striker Johnbosco Kalu can’t get the ball behind Maccabi Tel Aviv ’keeper Ofek Melika during the clubs’ 0-0 draw at Teddy Stadium. (photo credit: YEHUDA HALICKMAN) Beitar Jerusalem and Maccabi Tel Aviv battled to a thrilling 0-0 draw at Teddy Stadium, while Hapoel Tel Aviv overcame a third-minute red card to claim a dramatic 1-0 victory. Beitar Jerusalem and Maccabi Tel Aviv played to an entertaining 0-0 draw at Teddy Stadium, while Hapoel Tel Aviv overcame an early red card to defeat Ironi Tiberias 1-0 in a dramatic round of Israeli Premier League action. Elsewhere, Maccabi Haifa came from behind to beat Maccabi Petah Tikva 2-1, Hapoel Beersheba scored twice late to defeat Hapoel Jerusalem by the same score, Maccabi Netanya edged Kiryat Shmona 1-0, Hapoel Ramat Gan beat Hapoel Haifa 2-0, and Bnei Sakhnin defeated Hapoel Petah Tikva 2-0. More than 30,000 fans packed Teddy Stadium as Beitar and Maccabi renewed their rivalry in a crucial early-season clash between two title contenders. The match also marked Beitar’s long-awaited return to its home ground after spending the summer playing at Bloomfield Stadium while a new hybrid pitch was installed. Maccabi started aggressively, with Helio Varela involved in dangerous attacks that saw Dor Peretz and Sagiv Yehezkel come close. Varela later unleashed a powerful strike that narrowly missed the target, while Beitar gradually found its rhythm and began creating chances of its own. Yarden Shua supplied a superb through ball to Johnbosco Kalu, whose off-balance effort struck the woodwork. Boris Enow also missed a promising opportunity as the teams went into halftime scoreless. The Israeli Premier League soccer match between Hapoel Tel Aviv and Ironi Tiberias at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv, October 17, 2026. (credit: Danny Maron/Flash90) The chances continued after the break, with Shua, Tomer Yosefi and Omer Atzily all threatening for Beitar. Atzily missed a clear chance in the 73rd minute, sending a point-blank effort over the crossbar. Maccabi also had chances, but the defining moment came when Peretz appeared to have an open goal. With Beitar goalkeeper Miguel Silva caught well off his line, Brayan Carabali recovered in time to clear Peretz’s effort off the goal line with a remarkable kick save. Neither side could find a breakthrough, so the teams settled for a point in a match that delivered plenty of excitement but no goals. (photo credit: YEHUDA HALICKMAN) Beitar Jerusalem and Maccabi Tel Aviv battled to a thrilling 0-0 draw at Teddy Stadium, while Hapoel Tel Aviv overcame a third-minute red card to claim a dramatic 1-0 victory. Beitar Jerusalem and Maccabi Tel Aviv played to an entertaining 0-0 draw at Teddy Stadium, while Hapoel Tel Aviv overcame an early red card to defeat Ironi Tiberias 1-0 in a dramatic round of Israeli Premier League action. Elsewhere, Maccabi Haifa came from behind to beat Maccabi Petah Tikva 2-1, Hapoel Beersheba scored twice late to defeat Hapoel Jerusalem by the same score, Maccabi Netanya edged Kiryat Shmona 1-0, Hapoel Ramat Gan beat Hapoel Haifa 2-0, and Bnei Sakhnin defeated Hapoel Petah Tikva 2-0. More than 30,000 fans packed Teddy Stadium as Beitar and Maccabi renewed their rivalry in a crucial early-season clash between two title contenders. The match also marked Beitar’s long-awaited return to its home ground after spending the summer playing at Bloomfield Stadium while a new hybrid pitch was installed. Maccabi started aggressively, with Helio Varela involved in dangerous attacks that saw Dor Peretz and Sagiv Yehezkel come close. Varela later unleashed a powerful strike that narrowly missed the target, while Beitar gradually found its rhythm and began creating chances of its own. Yarden Shua supplied a superb through ball to Johnbosco Kalu, whose off-balance effort struck the woodwork. Boris Enow also missed a promising opportunity as the teams went into halftime scoreless. The Israeli Premier League soccer match between Hapoel Tel Aviv and Ironi Tiberias at Bloomfield Stadium in Tel Aviv, October 17, 2026. (credit: Danny Maron/Flash90) The chances continued after the break, with Shua, Tomer Yosefi and Omer Atzily all threatening for Beitar. Atzily missed a clear chance in the 73rd minute, sending a point-blank effort over the crossbar. Maccabi also had chances, but the defining moment came when Peretz appeared to have an open goal. With Beitar goalkeeper Miguel Silva caught well off his line, Brayan Carabali recovered in time to clear Peretz’s effort off the goal line with a remarkable kick save. Neither side could find a breakthrough, so the teams settled for a point in a match that delivered plenty of excitement but no goals. Ten-man Hapoel Tel Aviv battles to dramatic victory over Ironi Tiberias Hapoel Tel Aviv, meanwhile, earned a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Ironi Tiberias despite playing almost the entire match with 10 men. Wearing pink shirts to mark Breast Cancer Month, the Reds suffered an early setback when Andrian Kraev was sent off in the third minute for stomping on David Keltjens’ leg. Hapoel continued to push forward despite the numerical disadvantage, although the teams went into halftime scoreless after a potential penalty appeal involving Chico was rejected following a VAR review. The match took another turn in the 57th minute when Emmanuel Boateng and Ziv Morgan collided heads, leaving Boateng requiring a stretcher to leave the pitch with an injury above his left eye. Hapoel finally found the breakthrough with 10 minutes remaining. Marcus Coco surged into the penalty area and was brought down by goalkeeper Ido Sharon, earning a spot kick that Omri Altman converted to secure the victory. “We knew after the red card that the game would be very difficult and that we would have to give extra, and everyone did that,” Hapoel coach Elyaniv Barda said. “We gained a lot from this, especially in terms of the players’ mentality. Even with 10 men, we believed we could win.” Altman dedicated the victory to Kraev, saying the team wanted to help lift his spirits after the early dismissal. Tiberias coach Alon Ziv expressed frustration that his team failed to exploit its numerical advantage, while Sharon questioned the penalty decision. Maccabi Haifa stages comeback victory over Maccabi Petah Tikva Maccabi Haifa also rallied from behind, scoring twice from corner kicks to defeat Maccabi Petah Tikva 2-1. Petah Tikva took an early lead through Eyal Einbrom’s finish from inside the box, but Eitan Azoulay and Noam Sztejfman headed home in the second half to turn the match around. Haifa coach Barak Bachar praised his team’s resilience after coming back to win for the third straight game. “It wasn’t a great performance; there was a little luck involved, and we came under pressure in the final minutes,” Bachar said. “It was a difficult game against a team that sat deep, on a challenging pitch, and I’m happy we secured an important win in a tough match.” Petah Tikva coach Ziv Arie was disappointed that his team’s work was undone by set pieces, while Sztejfman described scoring the winner as a dream come true. Hapoel Beersheba produced another late turnaround, defeating Hapoel Jerusalem 2-1 through Igor Zlatanovic’s brace. Jerusalem took the lead when Vitalie Damascan went coast to coast before beating goalkeeper Ofir Marciano. Be’er Sheva responded in the 74th minute when Zlatanovic pounced on a rebound from Javon East. Ten minutes later, East was brought down in the penalty area, earning a spot kick and a red card for Jerusalem’s Ofek Nadir. Zlatanovic converted the penalty to complete the comeback and secure all three points. Beersheba coach Ran Kozuk emphasized the importance of his team’s determination, particularly late in the match, while Jerusalem coach Lior Zada acknowledged the challenge of defending against the combination of East and Zlatanovic. Maccabi Netanya claimed a narrow 1-0 win over Ironi Kiryat Shmona after Matheus Davo converted a second-half penalty. The spot kick was awarded following a Niv Gabbay handball in the box. Netanya coach Roni Levy said his team had created several clear-cut chances early but needed determination to secure the result. Kiryat Shmona coach Shai Barda lamented his side’s missed opportunities and said the team needed to find a way to reverse its difficult run. Hapoel Ramat Gan capitalizes on red card to defeat Hapoel Haifa 2-0 Hapoel Ramat Gan defeated Hapoel Haifa 2-0 after a second-half red card changed the contest. Haifa was reduced to 10 men in the 57th minute when Cheikh Keita was dismissed for a reckless foul. Ramat Gan capitalized almost immediately, with David Asanka scoring his first league goal two minutes later. Luan added the second in the 69th minute. Ramat Gan coach Messay Dego praised his players for responding well after a previous defeat, while Haifa coach Haim Silvas said his team had been unable to find solutions after going a man down. Bnei Sakhnin rounded out the round with a 2-0 victory over Hapoel Petah Tikva. Ahmed Salman scored in the first half before Mathew Cudjoe added another after the break. Sakhnin coach Yossi Abukasis credited the team’s improvement to reinforcements, a more settled lineup and growing confidence. Petah Tikva coach Omer Peretz said his team had controlled much of the contest statistically but failed to make its opportunities count. See more Israeli sports coverage at www.sportsrabbi.com/en

item.title: Kraken Beat Back Red Wings in First Game of Road Trip
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings , in their only US-based game on their four game road trip came away with a point after losing to the Seattle Kraken 4-3 following the shootout. Despite a heroic third period rally, including Alex DeBrincat ’s 300th career goal, the Red Wings were ultimately unable to push past Philipp Grubauer and the Seattle Kraken. Bobby McMann hit the game deciding goal in the fourth frame of the shootout to seal the game, leaving the Red Wings winless against the Kraken for the season. Raymond getting revved up The Red Wings found themselves down early in the game, with Mackie Samoskevich, Ryker Evans and Brandon Montour sneaking the puck past Daniil Tarasov before Detroit responded on the scoreboard. Detroit looked sluggish for much of the game, with Seattle dominating play in the Red Wings o-zone for much of the first and second period. However, as the third period wore on, the Red Wings were able to find some momentum off the back of Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond scoring two goals in 59 seconds a little over halfway through the period. Arvidsson broke Seattle’s momentum with his first 5v5 goal in a Red Wings uniform to make the score 3-1. Raymond potted the game winner in Detroit’s shootout win over the San Jose Sharks last Saturday. However, the young winger had gone the first nine games of the season without notching a tally in the goal column on the scoresheet before tonight. The dam looks to have opened though, with Raymond collecting his own rebound and using some slick stick handling moves to deposit the puck in behind Grubauer to bring the Red Wings within one of the Kraken tonight. Both Arvidsson and Raymond have had somewhat slow starts to their seasons, however, the two wingers managed to spark some life back into the Red Wings tonight, even if the rally ultimately fell short. Cat has some tricks in the bag Still, the Red Wings needed a little extra help to force overtime tonight. Facing down the prospect of snapping their four game points-streak, head coach Todd McLellan pulled Tarasov to give Detroit the extra skater late in the third period. The Kraken would only add to their own plight when Chandler Stephenson was put in the penalty box with a little under a minute and a half left in regulation, giving the Red Wings a 6-on-4 situation. As the clock ticked down in the final minute of the game, the Red Wings turned to their best player, and DeBrincat snapped the puck in on a wrist shot behind Grubauer to tie the game with just 16 seconds left. He, alongside sophomore center Emmitt Finnie , figured into all three of Detroit’s goals tonight. DeBrincat added to his totals to take the team lead in both goals (6) and assists (5) amongst Red Wings skaters tonight. item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings , in their only US-based game on their four game road trip came away with a point after losing to the Seattle Kraken 4-3 following the shootout. Despite a heroic third period rally, including Alex DeBrincat ’s 300th career goal, the Red Wings were ultimately unable to push past Philipp Grubauer and the Seattle Kraken. Bobby McMann hit the game deciding goal in the fourth frame of the shootout to seal the game, leaving the Red Wings winless against the Kraken for the season. Raymond getting revved up The Red Wings found themselves down early in the game, with Mackie Samoskevich, Ryker Evans and Brandon Montour sneaking the puck past Daniil Tarasov before Detroit responded on the scoreboard. Detroit looked sluggish for much of the game, with Seattle dominating play in the Red Wings o-zone for much of the first and second period. However, as the third period wore on, the Red Wings were able to find some momentum off the back of Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond scoring two goals in 59 seconds a little over halfway through the period. Arvidsson broke Seattle’s momentum with his first 5v5 goal in a Red Wings uniform to make the score 3-1. Raymond potted the game winner in Detroit’s shootout win over the San Jose Sharks last Saturday. However, the young winger had gone the first nine games of the season without notching a tally in the goal column on the scoresheet before tonight. The dam looks to have opened though, with Raymond collecting his own rebound and using some slick stick handling moves to deposit the puck in behind Grubauer to bring the Red Wings within one of the Kraken tonight. Both Arvidsson and Raymond have had somewhat slow starts to their seasons, however, the two wingers managed to spark some life back into the Red Wings tonight, even if the rally ultimately fell short. item.title: Blue Jackets’ Rick Bowness drops unreal reaction to blowout Maple Leafs loss
item.description: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images Blue Jackets’ Rick Bowness drops unreal reaction to blowout Maple Leafs loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Columbus Blue Jackets took on the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday night. Columbus had a bit of motivation, as this was Kirill Marchenko’s first game against the Blue Jackets following his trade to the Maple Leafs before the season started. Despite the motivation, Rick Bowness watched his team come out quite flat. The Maple Leafs won by a score of 6-2 on Tuesday night. Marchenko scored a goal against his former team to help in the effort. After the game, Bowness made a rather unreal admission about his team’s performance against Toronto. “I didn’t see that coming. We had good meetings today and thought we were ready to go. We made it a little too easy on their top-end guys. They made us pay the price,” the Blue Jackets head coach said, via The Hockey Writers reporter Mark Scheig. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Columbus got on the board first, and did so quite early. Jake Christiansen scored his first goal of the season a little more than two minutes in to make it a 1-0 game. However, Marchenko tied the game with a power-play goal four minutes later. From there, it was all Toronto. They scored five unanswered goals to make quick work of the Blue Jackets. Columbus has fallen to 3-5-0 on the 2026-27 campaign as a result of this loss. This was certainly not the outcome anyone wanted, especially Bowness. The veteran head coach will need to kick his team into gear once again moving forward. The Blue Jackets take the ice again on October 24 when they face the Vegas Golden Knights.

item.title: Manchester City have unlocked a new level of danger with Phil Foden firing
item.description: Manchester City have unlocked a new level of danger with Phil Foden firing Phil Foden broke his goalscoring duck when he scored the opening goal for Manchester City in their 3-2 win over Ipswich Town last Saturday. That goal, and Foden’s performance, showed that he was close to finding his touch once again. Following on from that display, Foden scored a hat-trick last night as Enzo Maresca’s side beat AEK Athens 5-1 in their UEFA Champions League league phase fixture at the Etihad Stadium. With Foden firing, the Manchester City attack is infinitely more dangerous, which was on display against AEK Athens. The class of Phil Foden stood out as Manchester City brushed AEK Athens aside. It was impossible to miss the class of Phil Foden’s performance against AEK Athens. Outside of his hat-trick, the class of Foden was evident throughout City’s win. Foden was crisp in possession, elusive when on the ball and his link-up play with his teammates, especially Rico Lewis, was superb. To top it off, Phil Foden scored a brilliant hat-trick. His first goal came after a powerful finish in the 34th minute after he combined with Rico Lewis on City’s right-hand side to give his team a 2-0 lead. Phil Foden’s second goal came via a thumping first-time finish after Rayan Cherki played a ball over the AEK Athens defence and Rico Lewis laid the ball back for Foden to hit with a sublime piece of control and skill. Foden would complete his hat-trick after he tapped in a Ryan McAidoo cross at the back post to cap off a move which was born in Manchester City’s academy. Phil Foden also grabbed an assist as it was his lay off that set up Rayan Cherki to score Manchester City’s third goal of the night. Last night’s performance from Phil Foden was the England international at his best. His finishing was on point, as was his touch in possession and movement. With Foden playing like he has in his past two matches, Enzo Maresca’s side has another element added to their attack. Enzo Maresca’s side is a more dangerous threat in the final third with Foden firing. Manchester City are blessed with wide variety of attacking options. Each of City’s attacking players offers something unique in the final third. However, it isn’t a stretch to say that City are at their most dangerous when they have Foden firing. He is an elite finisher and his game combines superbly well with his teammates. In a team blessed with quality, guile, power and speed Foden offers a different threat entirely to anyone else in the Manchester City squad. He has now scored four goals in his past two matches which illustrates what a firing Phil Foden brings to the table. Speaking after last night’s match, Enzo Maresca revealed that he has been thrilled with Phil Foden’s form before his red card against Manchester United last month. item.title: 'He deserves that trophy' - Serge Gnabry backs Bayern Munich team-mate Harry Kane to win Ballon d'Or ahead of Arsenal Champions League clash
item.description: German winger endorses prolific striker Gnabry has backed the Bavarians' focal point to claim the game's most prestigious individual prize ahead of Wednesday night's league-phase encounter against his old employers . The 33-year-old frontman is competing with Barcelona's La Liga and World Cup winner, Lamine Yamal, for the honour. His case is built on an astonishing 61-goal club haul that delivered last season's Bundesliga title alongside captaining England to the World Cup semi-finals against Argentina. Consistent output sets high standard The England skipper has carried that momentum into the 2026-27 campaign by registering nine goals and six assists across 10 appearances in all competitions, including three strikes in two Champions League outings. Those contributions have helped keep his side at the Bundesliga summit on 14 points, level with Borussia Dortmund. Explaining to TNT Sports why his colleague merits the accolade this year, Gnabry said: "He's shown it time and time again, how valuable he is. How much he has improved since coming here - an incredible player. "Very deserving. I said it earlier at a press conference. I don't know who decides the markers on who deserves to win that trophy, but he has had an incredible year. He's still in great form, still scoring a lot of goals, so valuable to our team. I would wish it for him, he deserves that trophy." Asked what it means to play alongside the forward in Munich, he described him as a "big example" before adding: "He scores a lot of goals. The right mindset, he's always in the game, focused. In that sense, a calm through the storm, and sets the bar high." Former Gunner praises North London Wednesday's fixture also pits Gnabry against the club he departed in 2016 after struggling for opportunities under Arsene Wenger, joining Werder Bremen before sealing a switch to Bavaria a year later and spending the 2017-18 campaign on loan at TSG Hoffenheim. Having shared a dressing room with Mikel Arteta during his spell in north London, he will now come up against the Spaniard as an opposing manager. Hailing the impressive transformation and title success overseen by his former team-mate last term, Gnabry explained: "It wasn't an easy project. For him to last that long, to have that success, and make them champions again, is a very big achievement. Probably a bigger achievement than some achievements by bigger coaches. "I've played for the club, so in some ways I'm happy for them, but of course, tomorrow, I'm playing for Bayern Munich. They're my current club, and we need to win tomorrow." London ceremony follows European test London ceremony follows European test Once Wednesday's heavyweight continental tie concludes, attention will quickly shift to the Ballon d'Or ceremony on Monday, October 26 . Beyond discovering whether he takes home the golden ball, Kane is also expected to clarify his long-term club future in the coming weeks. item.title: Donald Trump party member reminds Cathy Engelbert of ‘common sense’ after WNBA rejects Enes Kanter
item.description: Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The WNBA’s final decision on Enes Kanter has led to one Republican Party member taking a shot at Cathy Engelbert. Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom’s dream of playing in the WNBA has been shattered after the league officially rejected his request to enter the 2027 draft. As expected, the WNBA cited that Kanter, being a biological male, cannot participate in the league, and hence, he’s ineligible for the next season’s draft. It may seem like a pretty straightforward response, but it has led to soon-to-be retired WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert being called out by a member of Donald Trump’s Republican Party. Republican Party politician calls out the WNBA’s lack of definition on who can play in the league The only reason Kanter even submitted his name for 2027 WNBA Draft consideration was due to the league’s reluctance to give a clear definition of what a female is. It sparked massive outrage from fans amid the potential participation of transgender athletes in the W. Now, even though the WNBA has rejected Kanter’s submission, Republican Party politician Mark Harris has taken a shot at Engelbert. “By denying Enes Kanter’s eligibility, the WNBA admits that biological s__ determines gender. Yet the league still has no clear standard defining who can compete,” Harris wrote on X . He added, “It’s common sense, and exactly why I called on Commissioner Cathy Engelbert to establish one last month.” It seems that Engelbert cannot escape controversy during the final leg of her stint as the WNBA Commissioner. However, this could have all been avoided if the league had given a clear response about which gender can play in the W instead of playing it safe. item.title: Pistons’ Jalen Duren revels what fueled 22-point comeback victory over Celtics
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Pistons’ Jalen Duren revels what fueled 22-point comeback victory over Celtics appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A “never say die” mentality continues to define the Detroit Pistons . They found themselves in troubled waters, down by double digits during their regular-season home opener. However, the Pistons climbed out of a 22-point deficit and defeated the Boston Celtics 121-113. The matchup started with a close, back-and-forth first quarter. After a sluggish second quarter and beginning of the third period, the Pistons played their best ball in the second half. Detroit outscored Boston 76-55 in the final two periods, which included a 23-0 run. All-Star center Jalen Duren detailed in the media postgame session what helped the Pistons get out of their slump against the Celtics. “The comeback embodies our culture and what we’re trying to build here. We’re a team that is known to be gritty, known to get it out of the mud, known to never quit, and that’s our identity,” Duren explained. “Even the guys who are new here are embodying that, and that’s why we were able to have the outcome we had.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Detroit went ice cold offensively during the second quarter to help create their deficit. They were only able to connect on 6-of-22 shots from the field and 2-of-10 from 3-point range. The Pistons also had to withstand a prime performance from forward Paul George, who scored a game-high 38 points. Duren played a big part in the team effort for the comeback victory. The All-NBA center ended the contest with 22 points and nine rebounds in 28 minutes of action. Six of those rebounds came on the defensive end, and the other three were from the offensive glass. These statement wins point to Detroit’s identity. Duren addressed the team’s mental makeup to the media and how they are built to survive big deficits in order to find a path to victory. “We’re not the team to hang our heads. We’ve seen the bottom. A lot of guys are new here, but we’ve seen the bottom, so we’re not afraid of it. We fight, man,” Duren said. “That’s the identity of our team. … I’d never say we were scared or worried or anything. We knew we had to pick it up and play our brand of basketball to get back in it.” The Pistons had five different players finish in double-digit scoring. All-Star point guard Cade Cunningham also scored 22 points with eight assists. Shooting guard Duncan Robinson added 21 points for the Pistons while knocking down five triples.
