item.title: 'He has lost': Skip Bayless says he just has one takeaway from LeBron James' 76ers debut
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images Skip Bayless has delivered his instant reaction to LeBron James’ Philadelphia 76ers debut against the New York Knicks. It was a special night for the defending NBA champions as they were set to receive their rings, but their party was spoiled by the Sixers. James finally won a debut game in the NBA, after failing to do so on four previous occasions. There was a lot to like about his performance, but Bayless has highlighted a potential concern. Skip Bayless says LeBron James has ‘lost his athleticism’ One of James’ greatest strengths throughout his career in the NBA has been his athleticism. In his prime, ‘The King’ was almost unstoppable, but as you would expect from a 41-year-old now, there is a drop in his physical level. Bayless felt that was evident in James’s debut for the Philadelphia 76ers against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night. Nevertheless, Bayless liked most of what he saw from the veteran and showered praise on him. He said in a video posted on X: “Hey, I must admit pretty good opening night for LeBron James. His first game as a Sixer. This went at Madison Square Garden on ring night for the Knicks. Ring nights are often distracting and draining. “LeBron did play 34 minutes, a little longer than I thought he would. He did score 14 points. He did have, surprisingly, nine rebounds. He can still bully ball at going on age 42 (currently 41). I was surprised he had only seven assists. I think he can average 10 or 11 and lead the league in assists this year. “He’ll find his way. He’ll find his vibe with his new teammates. Only one turnover, that’s extraordinary from him. 0 for 3 from 3 is typical, predictable. Remember he shot 31.7% from 3 last year as a Laker. That was third from the bottom in the NBA. But he did make a couple of defensive plays. “My only takeaway from tonight was, man, he has lost a lot of athleticism. Again, going on age 42, your 24th (year), but it just surprised me tonight. He doesn’t have that much explosive lift anymore. That one jumper that he made just looked awkward to me. But who cares? “I’ve told you he has got to become a pass-first point guard. Orchestrate, run the show. Make sure Jaylen Brown is happy, which is hard. He’s a hard guy to keep happy. Make sure that Maxie is the star of the team. He showed it again tonight with 28. Keep Joel involved.” After a winning start, the Sixers take on the Cleveland Cavaliers next. James has an excellent record against his hometown side, winning 76 per cent of his games. item.title: Mitch Johnson comes to Victor Wembanyama's defense after an atrocious season opener
item.description: Mitch Johnson comes to Victor Wembanyama's defense after an atrocious season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After the San Antonio Spurs ' impressive run to the 2026 NBA Finals, all eyes have been on them. They had a tough first test to start the 2026-27 season because they just lost to their bitter rivals, the Oklahoma City Thunder . It was a tough defeat, especially because Victor Wembanyama struggled mightily. Wembanyama went 1-for-13 from the field, so he got most of his 12 points from the free-throw line. It was a bad night for him offensively, but he was still an intimidating defensive presence with his 13 rebounds, one steal, and six blocks. However, people also expect him to make an impact on offense. Mitch Johnson defends Victor Wembanyama after a terrible season opener On the other end of the floor, Wembanyama's MVP rival Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was dominant. He scored 32 points to lead his team to the victory, as he kept pouring in buckets from all over the court. It was a disappointing performance from the Spurs , especially because a lot of people see them as contenders. With this kind of flat performance, people might get discouraged about what the Spurs could do this season. This was only one game, but it has set the tone for the Western Conference's two giants. MORE: Victor Wembanyama and Jaylin Williams were at the center of a scuffle in the Spurs vs. Thunder season opener As the Spurs' head coach, Mitch Johnson was obviously disappointed in his team's performance. However, he did not want to single out Wembanyama for his inefficiencies because he thought the entire team did not show up properly for their season opener. "Thought we came out probably really amped up, which would be understandable. I don't think we put our energy or channel that energy in the right places. Execution was not good... I think everybody struggled equally. I know obviously his field goal will stand out, but everyone that participated in that," Johnson said after the loss to the Thunder . Of course, this is a big lesson for the Spurs. They are a fantastic team, but they are still learning. If they can cement themselves better, this would have been a much better performance. However, they do need their superstar to step up and prove why he's being considered as an MVP candidate. item.title: Sharks Locker Room: Celebrini Responds to Boos, Misa Snaps Slump, How Warsofsky Got San Jose Going
item.description: MONTREAL — The San Jose Sharks needed a win like this. The Sharks were down 3-1 in the third period and looked dead in the water. They weren’t generating a lot of scoring chances and were being hamstrung by porous defensive play. Canadien fans were piling on, booing Canadian hero Macklin Celebrini . But then, the San Jose captain responded and led his side to a galvanizing 4-3 OT victory. Celebrini scored twice, Michael Misa netted his first of the season, and Tyler Toffoli put in a brilliant Celebrini pass. Post-game, Celebrini talked about the boos, Toffoli shared more about Ryan Warsofsky’s fiery second intermission message, Misa discussed the rollercoaster sequence that led to him breaking his slump, and Warsofsky spoke on how proud he was of his team. Macklin Celebrini View this post on Instagram Celebrini, on if he heard the boos from the Bell Center crowd: How could I not? No, I mean, it was great. I’m just really happy we closed that one out. Celebrini, on if he’s used to boos: That was the first. That was the first. Warsofsky gave a fiery message during the second intermission. The message? Celebrini: “Get to our game, battle as hard as we can, and leave it all out there.” And a few other choice words, I bet! — Sheng Peng (@Sheng_Peng) October 21, 2026 Tyler Toffoli Toffoli, on San Jose Sharks head coach Warsofsky’s second intermission message: I think we all knew that we weren’t playing well enough, so obviously he came in and really emphasized that, and obviously whatever he was saying sparked us a little bit. Toffoli, on Misa breaking his slump: He’s done some really good things throughout the year. Everybody obviously just thinks about points and all that, but I think he’s been doing a pretty good job, and he’s finding his game. He’s still, it’s just his second year in the league, and he missed a lot of time last year, so he’s definitely going to be relied upon a lot more now with whatever Wenny’s dealing with, and hopefully continues to keep going and keep getting better and stepping up. Michael Misa View this post on Instagram Misa, on hitting a post, then scoring his first goal of the season: I mean, just a little frustrating at the time. I’ve been getting a little snakebit. I think when I caught [the pass from Kiefer Sherwood ], I knew, if I don’t score it, there’s something wrong with me. Ryan Warsofsky Warsofsky, on what he said to the San Jose Sharks in the second intermission: It’s not about me. It’s about the players and just getting them to understand how we need to play. item.title: I had one of my best competitive years in 2026. Here's how my gear helped me
item.description: The Qi4D driver with the Fujikura Ventus TR Black was a nice addition to my bag this year. Jack Hirsh/GOLF This past year, I had perhaps my best competitive season since high school, and a big reason was the new trust I had in my equipment. This season, I shot 71 twice, made an albatross, got my handicap index back below 1.0, and qualified for my first state amateur or mid-amateur in five years. The journey started, though, when we embarked on Fully Fit, a fitting bonanza that gave me the chance to get fit by six OEMs and decide what clubs would make it into my bag for the upcoming year. While I had been GOLF’s gear editor for about a year, I still had yet to take that kind of holistic look at my entire golf bag with each OEM. In fact, at that point, I had had a full bag fitting with just two of them. It’s not so much that I had any gaping holes in my bag, but there was so much I hadn’t tried. While many of my fittings ended up in product that I would have expected, other spots I tried something new. How my gear helped my game in 2026 For me, no change from this year ended up being as significant as my iron shaft change to the Nippon N.S.Pro Modus3 Tour 120 X paired with Cobra’s 3DP iron platform . Before TaylorMade’s Brandon Dooley and Cobra’s Andrew Lusty fit me into that unique and softer profile shaft, every fitting I had ever done resulted in the stout Project X 6.5. What was the result? This summer, I had the best competitive run in my career, including shooting 71 twice in tournament rounds, making a solid run at match play in my club championship again and qualifying for my first state amateur, the Pennsylvania Mid-Amateur, in five years. Having the slightly softer iron shaft introduced an element of feel that not only helped me drastically reduce my feared left miss, but it also allowed me to be more creative with my shot-making and even add a left-to-right ball flight I never had before. The shaft combined with the remarkable forgiveness of Cobra’s 3DP platform allowed me to hit some incredible iron shots, including my first-ever albatross in June. I also got in a position with my wedges that left me with absolutely no fear around the greens. Titleist TPI fitter Louis Raynard moved me into Vokey’s M-grind and eventually the WedgeWorks A+ grind in the lob wedge when it was released. During my PA Mid-Am qualifier in August, for the first time in competition, I got up and down on each one of my five missed greens on my way to qualifying. My final 2026 WITB Ball : Titleist ’25 Pro V1 Enhanced Alignment Driver: TaylorMade Qi4D 9.0˚ (Fujikura Ventus TR Black+ 7-X) Mini driver: TaylorMade R7 Quad Mini 13.5˚ (Fujikura Ventus TR Blue 7-X) Hybrid*: Ping G440 20˚ (Fujikura Ventus Blue HB+ 9-X) 7-wood* : Titleist GT1 4-Hybrid 20˚ (Fujikura Ventus Blue HB+ 9-X) Utility Iron*: Titleist U505 20˚ (Project X HZRDUS 80 6.5) Irons: Cobra 3DP Tour (4), 3DP MB (5-9) (Nippon N.S.Pro Modus3 Tour 120 X) Wedges: Titleist Vokey SM11 (46.10F, 50.12F, 54.14F @ 55, 60A+) (Nippon N.S.Pro Modus3 Tour 120 X, Project X Wedge 6.5) Putter: Ping Scottsdale TEC Ally Blue Onset * Utility iron, hybrid and 7-wood based on course/conditions What clubs helped me the most in 2026 7-wood (4-hybrid) Jack Hirsh/GOLF Head: Titleist GT1 20˚ Shaft: Fujikura Ventus Blue HB+ 9-X Loft: 20˚ @ 19˚ SureFit setting: D1 SureFit CG : 5g front, 11g rear Length: 40.5″ EOG Tipping: .5″ Swingweight: D3 Why it mattered: As someone who struggled to find a reliable and versatile third tee club for a long time, I never thought I’d find it in a game improvement hybrid, but it actually makes a lot of sense. The Titleist GT1 hybrid’s oversized profile made it perfect for me as a compact 7-wood option that gave me something I could dig out of rough and hit it high. It also proved useful off the tee on many of the short courses I played throughout the season in competition. The GT1 served a valuable role in my bag, alternating with my mid-flying hybrid and a utility iron. I also would be remiss not to call out my shaft change to the Fujikura Ventus Blue HB+. I was using a much heavier shaft in my hybrid to help battle the left miss, but it was causing my spin to drop, which wasn’t helping my hybrid land with any sort of control. When I was fit for the GT1, I also made the switch in my G440 hybrid and both clubs. Titleist GT1 Custom Hybrid $329.00 from Fairway Jockey View Product ALSO AVAILABLE AT: PGA TOUR Superstore , Titleist Irons 1 /2 Jack Hirsh/GOLF 2 /2 Jack Hirsh/GOLF Set composition: Cobra 3DP Tour (4), 3DP MB (5-9) Shafts: Nippon N.S.Pro Modus3 Tour 120 X Length: +.5″ (37.75″ 7-iron EOG) Lie: 2˚ Flat (60˚ 7-iron) Loft progression: 22.5/26/30/34/38/42 Swingweight: D2.5-D3 Why they mattered : What more can I say about my Cobra 3DP irons and Modus 120 X shafts? They never left my bag all year and gave me so much confidence to hit any shot between 160 and 220 yards. Cobra 3DP MB Custom Irons The 3DP MB iron combines the looks and feel of a traditional forged muscle back with the forgiveness of a cavity back iron. The most forgiving blade on the market, the MB has captivated Tour players by checking all the boxes and exceeding expectations with its exceptional stability and feel. FORGIVING MUSCLE BACK BLADE SHAPE A slightly revised shape from the KING MB inspired by feedback from PGA Tour player Max Homa, the MB features a thinned topline and enhanced offset. The internal 3D printed lattice and heel, toe and hosel tungsten increases MOI for stability, and positions the CG perfectly centered and lower than the KING MB to promote higher launch. EXTREME FORGIVENESS MEETS SOFT FEEL The 3D printed internal lattice structure not only optimizes weight savings, but also provides the stiffness and strength to support the face and fine-tune the acoustics of each iron to produce the most appealing impact sound and feel. TUNGSTEN WEIGHTING The discretionary weight savings from the 3D printed lattice allowed for up to 55g of tungsten to be positioned low in the heel, toe and hosel resulting in the perfect blend of a compact blade shape with a low CG and high MOI that mirrors a game improvement iron. $329.99 from Fairway Jockey View Product ALSO AVAILABLE AT: PGA Tour Superstore , Cobra Lob wedge Jack Hirsh/GOLF Heads: Titleist Vokey SM11 WedgeWorks Raw Lofts/grinds: 60A+ Shafts: Project X Wedge 6.5 Length: 35.5″ Lie: 62˚ Swingweight: D6.5 Why they mattered : When Fully Fit launched, the A+ Grind was not yet available, but Louis Raynard had a hunch this is where we’d end up. He was right. The A+ is a sibling of the M-Grind I was initially fit into, but with the ribbon on the sole ground off. This made it so my lob wedge glided through the bent grass I play in the Northeast much faster than the M. That’s not to say the M never sees my bag. I still use it whenever I head south to play off Bermuda. Raynard told me this how to do with the absence of the ribbon or the knuckle on the A+. In softer or dense turf, as I see in the Northeast, the smoother sole helps my wedge glide through the grass, but when the turf is firmer or less dense like Bermuda, the ribbon gives me some forgiveness to clip it. Titleist Vokey WedgeWorks SM11 A+ Grind Custom Wedge The A+ Grind is a mid-bounce wedge that originated from removing the grind lines from an M Grind — the same modification that turns an L Grind into an A. Because of this, the A+ moves faster through the turf than its related M Grind, but it features more bounce and a wider sole than the A. This helps the A+ Grind excel in firm to neutral conditions. “On tour over the years, we started seeing some loyal M Grind players who were finding that sole to be a little too bouncy for their liking,” said Dill. “Those players found the leading edge of the A+ sat a bit lower, and the wedge moved faster through the ground, unlocking a bit more versatility.” The 2013 Masters champion is one such player, regularly gaming a 58A+ on the PGA TOUR. $22

item.description: Motorsport photo Phillip Island will be making its final appearance on the MotoGP calendar this weekend as the venue for the Australian Grand Prix. Starting 2027, the iconic 4.4km track will be replaced by a modern version of the Adelaide street circuit. As such, one can expect a record crowd in Melbourne as the city bids goodbye to the premier class of motorcycle racing. The championship remains finely poised heading to the Australian GP, with just two points separating Jorge Martin (Aprilia) and Marc Marquez (Ducati) in the standings. Marco Bezzecchi, who returned to winning ways in Indonesia last time out, trails his team-mate Martin by 46 points, with Aprilia already admitting that it is considering issuing team orders sooner rather than later. item.title: A.J. Brown Apologizes to Teammate After Accidental Injury Mishap
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) Getty New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs was moved to IR on Monday after suffering a shoulder injury in the first quarter of the Week 6 win against the New York Jets. Whilst the injury itself was no doubt painful, having fallen on it awkwardly whilst hauling in a 42-yard touchdown reception, the actions following would have been no less so. After Doubs caught the touchdown and remained lying on the ground, teammate A.J. Brown grabbed him by the pads and trying to yank him up by his upper body, before eventually realizing that the former Green Bay Packer was hurt. A.J. Brown Apologizes to Romeo Doubs For Trying to Pull Him Up Speaking to the media on Tuesday regarding the incident, Brown shared that he apologized to Doubs following the incident. AJ Brown said he didn’t realize Romeo Doubs was hurt until after he picked him up and Doubs showed he was in discomfort. Brown said he apologized to Doubs for jostling him after he got hurt. — Ari Alexander (@AriA1exander) October 20, 2026 “AJ Brown said he didn’t realize Romeo Doubs was hurt until after he picked him up and Doubs showed he was in discomfort.” Ari Alexander posted on X on Tuesday. “Brown said he apologized to Doubs for jostling him after he got hurt.” Another X account, “Hater Report” posted video footage of the incident that shows Brown trying to pull Doubs up in order to celebrate the score. Romeo Doubs on the ground screaming for help and AJ Brown and DeMario Douglas manhandling him 😭 Doubs went on IR today 💀 pic.twitter.com/UXYjueSNbP — Hater Report (@HaterReport) October 19, 2026 Romeo Doubs Set to Spend At Least Next Month On Sidelines Now that the fifth year pro is on injured reserve, he will not see the field for at least the next four weeks, although ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported at the time on Monday that the team do not currently expect the absence to be “long term”. Doubs was already having a tough 2026 season; his first in New England after arriving on a four year, $68 million deal signed this offseason. Although he leads the Patriots in receiving yards, he’s managed only 261 total in his first five games. A fairly low number considering he has been the de facto WR1 since Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1. This past Sunday was his first game back since returning from IR. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post A.J. Brown Apologizes to Teammate After Accidental Injury Mishap appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 49ers game review: Mike Evans effect makes WR a weapon even when not targeted
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) carries the ball during the first half of a NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Santa Clara, Calif., Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Seconds before the San Francisco 49ers scored their first touchdown Monday night, ESPN analyst Troy Aikman used his telestrator to draw a yellow circle around wide receiver Mike Evans . Evans didn't score. But he was a reason tight end George Kittle did. Evans, on the outside left, ran a crossing route to the back of the end zone, attracting two Commanders defenders, which allowed Kittle, in the left slot, to easily exploit a mismatch: Kittle got behind linebacker Kain Medrano for his 11-yard snag in the left corner. Seconds before the 49ers scored their second touchdown, Aikman, again, drew a circle around Evans. It was 3rd-and-goal at the 1-yard line. Aikman was alerting viewers: Evans has scored 32 career touchdowns from inside the 5-yard line, including 10 1-yard scores. Evans didn't score. But was his deep red-zone history a reason running back Christian McCaffrey wasn't touched on his touchdown? The 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders was a fascinating illustration of the impact a player such as Evans can have. Not only on his own team's success, but also on an opponent's strategy. Evans played 22 snaps before he was forced to leave with Achilles tendinitis shortly before halftime. The 49ers averaged 9.3 yards per play with Evans on the field. On the 38 snaps Evans was off the field: 4.5 yards per play. Meanwhile, blitz-happy Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones was conservative when Evans was in the game. In the first half, Washington blitzed quarterback Brock Purdy on eight of his 24 dropbacks (33%), blitzing just twice when Evans was on the field. In the second half, Jones blitzed Purdy on seven of his 10 dropbacks (70%), twice sending two extra defenders. Was Kittle surprised by the lack of first-half pressure? "That's a great question," Kittle said. "I would say I was surprised that they didn't blitz as much in the first half. And then when they did it in the second half, we just didn't have an answer for it." The 49ers didn't have an answer partly because they didn't have Evans, who, at 6-foot-5 and 231 pounds, is a QB's best friend when under pressure. "It's almost like when a tight end is matched up on a smaller DB," Purdy said last week. "And you know, ‘I just got to get the ball in this guy's vicinity, and he's going to go up and get it.' I definitely feel that with him." Purdy didn't have anything resembling the same feeling with his four remaining healthy wideouts in the second half Monday. And that inspired Jones to keep sending more than four rushers, forcing Purdy to make quick decisions with some combination of Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing and Malik Turner on the field. Purdy has targeted that quartet with 13 passes this season (Evans has 39 targets). The 49ers' final three drives i
item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) carries the ball during the first half of a NFL football game against the Washington Commanders in Santa Clara, Calif., Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Seconds before the San Francisco 49ers scored their first touchdown Monday night, ESPN analyst Troy Aikman used his telestrator to draw a yellow circle around wide receiver Mike Evans . Evans didn't score. But he was a reason tight end George Kittle did. Evans, on the outside left, ran a crossing route to the back of the end zone, attracting two Commanders defenders, which allowed Kittle, in the left slot, to easily exploit a mismatch: Kittle got behind linebacker Kain Medrano for his 11-yard snag in the left corner. Seconds before the 49ers scored their second touchdown, Aikman, again, drew a circle around Evans. It was 3rd-and-goal at the 1-yard line. Aikman was alerting viewers: Evans has scored 32 career touchdowns from inside the 5-yard line, including 10 1-yard scores. Evans didn't score. But was his deep red-zone history a reason running back Christian McCaffrey wasn't touched on his touchdown? The 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders was a fascinating illustration of the impact a player such as Evans can have. Not only on his own team's success, but also on an opponent's strategy. Evans played 22 snaps before he was forced to leave with Achilles tendinitis shortly before halftime. The 49ers averaged 9.3 yards per play with Evans on the field. On the 38 snaps Evans was off the field: 4.5 yards per play. Meanwhile, blitz-happy Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones was conservative when Evans was in the game. In the first half, Washington blitzed quarterback Brock Purdy on eight of his 24 dropbacks (33%), blitzing just twice when Evans was on the field. In the second half, Jones blitzed Purdy on seven of his 10 dropbacks (70%), twice sending two extra defenders. Was Kittle surprised by the lack of first-half pressure? "That's a great question," Kittle said. "I would say I was surprised that they didn't blitz as much in the first half. And then when they did it in the second half, we just didn't have an answer for it." The 49ers didn't have an answer partly because they didn't have Evans, who, at 6-foot-5 and 231 pounds, is a QB's best friend when under pressure. "It's almost like when a tight end is matched up on a smaller DB," Purdy said last week. "And you know, ‘I just got to get the ball in this guy's vicinity, and he's going to go up and get it.' I definitely feel that with him." Purdy didn't have anything resembling the same feeling with his four remaining healthy wideouts in the second half Monday. And that inspired Jones to keep sending more than four rushers, forcing Purdy to make quick decisions with some combination of Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing and Malik Turner on the field. Purdy has targeted that quartet with 13 passes this season (Evans has 39 targets). The 49ers' final three drives included two sacks, no first downs and 7 net yards. On the five snaps on which Purdy was blitzed he was 0 for 2, dropped for two sacks and had a 6-yard scramble. With just over eight minutes left, on 2nd-and-4, right tackle Colton McKivitz looked inside to pick up blitzing linebacker Sonny Styles. The problem: No one blocked left defensive end Odafe Oweh, who wasn't touched before dropping Purdy for a 6-yard sack. On the next snap, Purdy rushed a throw to McCaffrey despite having a clean pocket. McCaffrey just turned his head as the incompletion sailed past him. "Because of the pressure Washington's been able to get on him on the last couple possessions," Aikman said, "he turns it loose early." Purdy will likely be without Evans on Sunday when the 49ers visit Atlanta, and his other top wideouts - Deebo Samuel , Demarcus Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling - will remain sidelined. Once Evans exited, Jones began blitzing an offense with a barren wide receiver corps. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich was presumably taking notes. • One of the biggest questions leading up to Sunday's game: What is the status of Upton Stout's right shoulder? The second-year slot corner was forced to leave after his shoulder injury was aggravated when he was blocked by tight end Ben Sinnott. After Stout grabbed at his shoulder with about 10 minutes left, he was replaced by Ashtyn Davis. And the dropoff was steep. Davis played 14 snaps. He missed two tackles, including a whiff on QB Jayden Daniels when he was unblocked on a blitz. Davis was also in coverage on wide receiver Treylon Burks' 30-yard reception, and he grabbed the back of wideout Antonio Williams' jersey, drawing an illegal contact penalty that wiped out a sack, on a 4th-and-8 play. Davis, 30, had only played special teams in the season's first five games. He's listed as a safety. Why did he replace Stout instead of moving outside cornerback Deommodore Lenoir inside, where he has extensive experience, and replacing Lenoir with Jack Jones? Head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated Davis had received more of the first-team practice work at nickel back with Stout limited with a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 4. "We put (Lenoir) there a lot, but he didn't get as many of the reps," Shanahan said. "Then it's a chain reaction (to move Lenoir), so we thought Ashtyn could step it up and go in there and do his job. I thought he did a really good job at it." But he didn't. Davis had the lowest Pro Football Focus grade (27.7) of any 49ers defender. If Stout is unavailable against Atlanta, it would qualify as a surprise if Davis was given another shot. • Rookie pass rusher Romello Height had three tackles, four quarterback hits and split the game-sealing sack with Keion White that didn't allow Daniels to heave a Hail Mary. Not bad. And not even close to a reflection of Height's impact. The stat sheet didn't include that the third-round pick also drew two holding penalties as a pass rusher and had the fourth-down sack that was negated by Davis' penalty on Washington's penultimate drive. "It seemed like he was all over the place," Shanahan said. In the first quarter, right tackle Josh Conerly was flagged for holding Height. It set up a 2nd-and-17, which led to a punt two plays later. In the third quarter, left tackle Brandon Coleman held Height. It set up a 2nd-and-14, which led to a punt two plays later. • Shanahan appeared to be managing Evans' snap count. Until he stopped. After Evans played 14 of 26 snaps on the 49ers' first four drives, he played eight of the first nine snaps on their fifth possession, being forced to leave after he'd played eight straight snaps. Shortly before Evans limped to the locker room, he was on all fours on the field, as if doing a pushup, in an attempt to stretch out his aching Achilles during a Washington timeout. Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: How LA28 aims to stage 'the best Paralympic Games ever'
item.description: The Olympics have soared before in Los Angeles. In less than two years, the Paralympics will take flight from L.A. for the first time. LA28 hopes to raise the bar for the Paralympic movement when the Paralympic Games open on Aug. 15, 2028. Michael Kappeler/dpa The Olympics have soared before in Los Angeles. In less than two years, the Paralympics will take flight from L.A. for the first time. LA28 hopes to raise the bar for the Paralympic movement when the Paralympic Games open in SoFi Stadium on Aug. 15, 2028. The city that already changed the Olympic movement by hosting the most commercially successful Games ever in 1984 could leave an equally indelible mark on the Paralympic movement. "In the opening ceremony in two years' time, we will be about to witness the Paralympic Games that can really put our movement in a higher step," International Paralympic Committee president Andrew Parsons said, "in a higher position as a sport movement." While the Olympics were blossoming in L.A. in 1984, the Paralympics that year were hosted in New York and Stoke Mandeville, England in a patchwork plan that came to be known as the "Last-Minute Games" because a U.S.-based organizing committee failed to secure funding to host the Paralympic Games at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Forty years later, the Paris Paralympics solidified the movement's position as one of the largest sporting events in the world. The 2024 Paralympics sold 2.5 million tickets, the most for a Paralympic Games, and had a record 12,941 global broadcast hours. The overall live audience for the Paris Paralympics grew by 40% compared to 2021 and 117% from 2016. Seeing the Paralympics leaves a lasting impression on fans. item.content:encoded: The Olympics have soared before in Los Angeles. In less than two years, the Paralympics will take flight from L.A. for the first time. LA28 hopes to raise the bar for the Paralympic movement when the Paralympic Games open on Aug. 15, 2028. Michael Kappeler/dpa The Olympics have soared before in Los Angeles. In less than two years, the Paralympics will take flight from L.A. for the first time. LA28 hopes to raise the bar for the Paralympic movement when the Paralympic Games open in SoFi Stadium on Aug. 15, 2028. The city that already changed the Olympic movement by hosting the most commercially successful Games ever in 1984 could leave an equally indelible mark on the Paralympic movement. "In the opening ceremony in two years' time, we will be about to witness the Paralympic Games that can really put our movement in a higher step," International Paralympic Committee president Andrew Parsons said, "in a higher position as a sport movement." While the Olympics were blossoming in L.A. in 1984, the Paralympics that year were hosted in New York and Stoke Mandeville, England in a patchwork plan that came to be known as the "Last-Minute Games" because a U.S.-based organizing committee failed to secure funding to host the Paralympic Games at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Forty years later, the Paris Paralympics solidified the movement's position as one of the largest sporting events in the world. The 2024 Paralympics sold 2.5 million tickets, the most for a Paralympic Games, and had a record 12,941 global broadcast hours. The overall live audience for the Paris Paralympics grew by 40% compared to 2021 and 117% from 2016. Seeing the Paralympics leaves a lasting impression on fans. A Nielsen Sports study commissioned by the IPC found that 73% of people thought the Paris Paralympic Games positively changed their attitudes toward people with disabilities. LA28 wants to build on that momentum. "I really would love to see the change of perception of what people with disabilities can do, but also most importantly see the athletes perform," said Ileana Rodriguez, the LA28 vice president of Paralympic strategy and relations and a 2012 Paralympic swimmer. "Because oftentimes we forget the sport side of the athletes and put the disability in front, and I really hope that this is reversed in our Games." It didn't take long for Ali Truwit to see the Paralympic standard. The former Yale swimmer had always respected Paralympians for their grit, courage and strength, but after she lost the lower part of her left leg in a shark attack in 2023, Truwit had her own Paralympic awakening. She realized that to even make the U.S. team for Paris, she needed to swim faster with one leg than she did with two. "A lot of people would come up and say, like, "Oh well you could do the Paralympics,'" said Truwit, who had 15 months between having her leg amputated on her 23rd birthday and the opening ceremony of the Paris Paralympics. "I'm like, 'Well, you can't just do the Paralympics actually!' It's elite and it's fast." Her American record time of 1 minute, 8.98 seconds seconds in the S10 100-meter backstroke at the 2024 U.S. Paralympic swimming trials was faster than the times she was putting up to be recruited for Division I schools. Also the U.S. record holder in the S10 400-meter freestyle (4:31.39), Truwit won silver medals in both races in her first Paralympic Games. But as she starts training for 2028, Truwit knows even her national record times might not be enough to get on the podium in L.A. In Paris, 175 world and 218 Paralympic records were broken across 22 sports. The quality of the performances are better than ever, Parsons, the Paralympic president, pointed out. Athletes have become more refined with their training techniques. "If you raise the expectations for what high performance is, for what an athlete is, then gosh, that's just going to open up so many more opportunities," said Brent Hardin, an associate professor of kinesiology at the University of Alabama and director of Alabama Adapted Athletics. "The Paralympics has the ability to do that like no other sporting event in the world for athletes with disabilities." The last time the Summer Paralympics were in the United States, in 1996, the event was run by a separate committee from the Olympic organizers. Disorganized and under-publicized, the event was underwhelming, Hardin said. Since 2002, organizing committees have been required to put together joint bids to host both the Olympic and Paralympic Games, using the same venues, facilities and infrastructure. LA28 will rely on mostly existing venues for both the Olympics and Paralympics, relieving many of the biggest headaches that have plagued previous organizing committees. But hosting 4,480 Paralympians in one village is an especially unique challenge. LA28 will host the Olympic and Paralympic villages at UCLA. While renowned for its red brick buildings and lush green lawns, UCLA's campus is also notorious for its steep hills. In 2025, two students who used wheelchairs sued the university and the UC Board of Regents for discrimination, citing, in part, elevators that are often out of service, insufficient signage and dangerous conditions in pedestrian paths of travel. Rodriquez recognized the campus' geographical challenges that organizers can't change. LA28 said in a statement it is focused on building upon UCLA's existing accessibility foundation while exploring additional modifications and services to support Paralympic athletes and team officials, such as temporary ramps and modified restrooms. Construction is expected to begin this year, trying to minimize impact on normal campus activities. "One solution is not going to solve it for everyone, but a system of different ones hopefully will for most of them," said Rodriguez, an architect consulted on previous Games before working with LA28. "We're aiming, of course, for 100% of the users, but it doesn't mean that there might be challenges in some points." The Games will also need to accommodate millions of fans traveling around Southern California. The FIFA World Cup tested the transportation system and it was largely a success, but it presented problems for some fans. Kate Scott, founder of Only Everywhere, a directory providing accessibility information about more than 400 venues in California, heard from fans who paid hundreds of extra dollars for accessible parking and a shuttle to the stadium only to learn later that a free shuttle option was available. Fans struggled to secure wheelchair accessible seats, especially after they were sold at astronomical resale values, and couldn't get clear answers about what accommodations would be available in the stadium. SoFi Stadium aced the physical infrastructure with working elevators, wheelchair escorts and accessible seating with clear sightlines on every level. It was mostly an information gap that left fans wanting. "It's not a problem if you say there's no way to get to the cafe on the second floor. It is a problem if they find that out at the bottom of the stairs," Scott said. "They can plan ahead if you just give them the information. It's not about perfection. It's about telling people what to expect." Of the 400 California venues Scott has added to Only Everywhere's directory, more than half don't publish anything online about accessibility. Only 7% cover accommodations for mobility limitation, hearing disability, vision impairment and sensory disabilities. Disability advocates hope the Paralympics can lead to improved access to social services and structures for people with disabilities during and after the Games. "Not just a one-in-every-four-years kind of event," said Juliann Anesi, an associate professor of gender studies at UCLA and an affiliate faculty member with the disabilities studies department. item.title: ‘Angel (Reese) Won That Game Before the Game Was Even Played’ — 5-Time All-Star Makes Striking Claim After Dream Level WNBA Finals
item.description: Kelsey Plum praises Angel Reese's mentality after her 30-point performance helps the Atlanta Dream level the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. Phoenix Mercury star Kelsey Plum believes Angel Reese’s mindset played a major role in the Atlanta Dream’s Game 2 victory over the Golden State Valkyries. The five-time All-Star discussed Reese’s approach and what it could mean for the rest of the WNBA Finals in a clip “Girls Tripp” posted Tuesday. The Dream won 79-65 Monday at Chase Center in San Francisco, with Reese finishing with 30 points and 16 rebounds. Two days earlier, she had gone scoreless in the second half of Atlanta’s 68-64 Game 1 loss. Kelsey Plum Praises Angel Reese’s Mentality After Game 2 Win Plum pointed to Reese’s determination when assessing Atlanta’s response to its series-opening loss. “Mentally, to me, she made a decision that she was going to win that game. And if you wanna get on the ship, the ship is moving. I think Angel won that game before the game was even played,” Plum said . Reese shot 10-for-16 and went 9-for-11 at the free-throw line in 34 minutes. She also had 3 assists and 2 blocks. Allisha Gray added 18 points, while Jordin Canada finished with 13 points and 10 assists. In Game 1, Reese scored 14 points on 5-for-8 shooting before halftime but missed all three of her attempts afterward and committed three turnovers. Atlanta managed just eight points in the fourth quarter. Reese acknowledged after the loss that she needed to look for her shots more. “I don’t think they really did anything. Maybe that was just on me. I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball, and trying to get the ball, and get to my spots. So definitely gonna do a better job of that next game.” She followed through Monday, helping Atlanta even the series before it heads home. Plum also questioned whether Golden State had anyone who could match Reese’s mentality over the remaining games. “Now, going throughout the series, the recipe is, like, ‘Okay, Angel has now set the bar.’ Who in Golden State is gonna match that? I don’t know who’s mentally strong enough, either individually or collectively, to be able to match that for Golden State.” Gabby Williams, who led the Valkyries with 26 points in Game 1, finished with 14 on 3-for-15 shooting Monday. Golden State committed 19 turnovers, while Atlanta recorded 14 steals and outscored the Valkyries 21-9 in the third quarter. SEE ALSO: ‘That’s an Issue’ – Valkyries Starters Put on Notice After Bench Outscores Them in Game 2 Loss to Angel Reese-Led Dream The Dream also held Golden State without a fast-break point while scoring 19 of their own. Atlanta went 30-for-35 at the free-throw line, compared with 11-for-16 for the Valkyries. Game 3 is scheduled for Wednesday at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, with Game 4 following Saturday at the same venue. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Third Period Costs Canuck Again In 6-3 Loss To The Hurricanes
item.description: The Vancouver Canucks fell 6-3 to the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday night at Rogers Arena. Linus Karlsson, Jonathan Lekkerimäki and Max Sasson found the back of the net while Leevi Meriläinen stopped 37 of the 42 shots he faced. With the loss, Vancouver's losing streak is now pushed to eight, with only one of those losses coming in overtime. A multi-goal third period against was once again made the difference for the Canucks. After heading into the final frame tied 3-3, Vancouver allowed three goals over the final 20 minutes which cost them the win. The Canucks have now allowed multiple goals in the third on five occasions, which includes each of the last three games. "It's a really good lesson for our group in that when your game lacks details in the third, or when you open up the door against teams that we've been playing, they make you pay," said Manny Malhotra post-game. "To be in the games, obviously, a lot of good things to be able to claw and scratch our way to stay in these games, but, it's a valuable lesson to us that 40s not good enough, 45s not good enough, 50s not good enough in this league. We have to stay with the process." The shot difference in this game was also staggering. While the Hurricanes constantly outshot the opposition, Vancouver managed only 17 shots compared to 43 against. Even though the Canucks were able to score three times, Tuesday was not a successful outing from an offensive perspective. Shifting over to positives, Meriläinen had yet another impressive performance in net. The Finnish goaltender kept Vancouver in the game and came up huge in the second period as he stopped Sebastian Aho on a penalty shot. If not for the play of Meriläinen, this game could have been a blowout early. The penalty kill also deserves some credit for the way they performed. The Canucks went five-for-five on the kill and allowed just eight shots against. Vancouver's power play also went one-for-two, making the night an overall success from a special teams perspective. Tuesday's loss was another reminder of how far the Canucks still need to go in their rebuild. While they had their moments, Carolina dominated play and showed why they are once again Stanley Cup contenders. Overall, Vancouver fought hard but couldn't find a way to pick up a win at Rogers Arena. item.title: Thunder center Aday Mara welcomes himself with an insane sequence vs. Victor Wembanyama
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images. Thunder center Aday Mara welcomes himself with an insane sequence vs. Victor Wembanyama appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma City Thunder rookie center Aday Mara delivered an impressive sequence against San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama during Tuesday night’s season opener at Frost Bank Center. Mara blocked Wembanyama at the rim before sprinting down the floor and finishing an alley-oop dunk off a pass from Thunder guard Ajay Mitchell. The sequence unfolded midway through the third quarter, with Oklahoma City holding an 82-70 advantage entering the play. Mara denied the Spurs star near the basket with approximately 4:22 remaining before completing the transition dunk roughly nine seconds later. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) ClutchPoints shared footage of the sequence on X, formerly Twitter, showcasing the rookie’s defensive stop and immediate offensive contribution against one of the NBA’s premier shot-blockers. Aday Mara MEETS Victor Wembanyama at the rim before running the floor for the slam 😤 pic.twitter.com/9M8KxEXC22 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 21, 2026 Mara entered his first NBA season after the Thunder selected him with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft following his collegiate career at Michigan. The 7-foot-3 center helped the Wolverines capture the 2026 national championship while earning Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year honors. During his final college season, Mara averaged 12.1 points, 6.8 rebounds and 2.6 blocks, establishing himself as one of the nation’s top interior defenders. His ability to protect the rim played a significant role in the Thunder’s decision to add him to their frontcourt. Tuesday’s sequence showcased those defensive skills against Wembanyama, while his connection with Mitchell demonstrated his effectiveness finishing in transition. The Thunder tipped off the 2026 season with established frontcourt contributors Isaiah Hartenstein and Chet Holmgren, giving Mara experienced teammates as he begins his NBA career. Mara’s block and subsequent alley-oop slam provided a highlight of Oklahoma City’s season opener against the Spurs on Tuesday night, with the Thunder leading 102-94 with 5:25 remaining in the fourth quarter. Related: Thunder star SGA gets 100% real on simple approach that helped OKC rip Spurs apart Related: Thunder HC Mark Daigneault speaks up on defense that Victor Wembanyama couldn’t solve

item.title: Horner reveals he nearly became Mercedes boss instead of Toto Wolff
item.description: Christian Horner has disclosed that he was given the chance to leave Red Bull for Mercedes at the end of 2012, with Niki Lauda attempting to convince him to take charge of the German manufacturer's Formula 1 operation. The revelation comes from Horner's memoir Drive, in which the former Red Bull team principal describes an approach from Lauda during the Christmas period. Despite the financial appeal of the proposal, Horner had little interest in walking away from the team he had led to three successive world championship doubles. Lauda approached Horner over Mercedes role By the end of 2012, Horner had established himself as one of Formula 1's most successful team principals. Red Bull had won both championships in each of the previous three seasons, with Sebastian Vettel emerging as the dominant figure in the team's rise to the top. Mercedes was in a very different position. Having returned to Formula 1 as a works team in 2010, the manufacturer was still working towards becoming a regular championship contender. Its ambitions were clear, however, with Lewis Hamilton already confirmed as a replacement for Michael Schumacher ahead of the 2013 campaign. As part of those plans, Lauda identified Horner as a potential candidate to lead the team. The three-time world champion approached the Briton at his home over Christmas, hoping to persuade him that a move to Mercedes would be worthwhile. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Horner was presented with an attractive financial package, but the prospect of leaving Red Bull was not something he was prepared to entertain. His relationship with the late Dietrich Mateschitz, who had entrusted him with running the team in 2005, played a decisive role in his response: "I feel a loyalty to Dietrich and the team, so as much as I appreciate this, I am not going to join Mercedes," Horner recalled. The rejection left Mercedes to pursue other options as it continued restructuring its Formula 1 management. Toto Wolff subsequently joined the German manufacturer in 2013, having previously been nvolved with Williams. Ross Brawn remained team principal that season, before Mercedes reorganised its leadership ahead of the introduction of Formula 1's new power unit regulations in 2014. The changes coincided with the beginning of an extraordinary period of success for Mercedes, which went on to secure eight consecutive constructors' championships between 2014 and 2021. Horner remained at Red Bull, overseeing Vettel's fourth successive title in 2013 before the team eventually returned to championship-winning form with Max Verstappen. Before agreeing to join Mercedes, the British driver explored the possibility of moving to Red Bull and attended a private meeting at Adrian Newey's home near Ascot. According to Horner, Hamilton considered Red Bull his preferred destination, but the prospect of putting him alongside Vettel was met with reservations from Helmut Marko. The considerable financial commitment required to sign the McLaren driver also contributed to Horner's decision not to pursue the deal.

item.title: Rebecca Jackson on life in male-dominated motorsport
item.description: Rebecca Jackson, from Portsmouth, says she's seen a surge in the number of female motor sport fans [Getty Images] When racing driver Rebecca Jackson first joined online car forums, she used only her surname to avoid being pre-judged for her gender. It was not until her first real-life meet that her cover was blown. "I got out of the car and they went, 'Oh, Jackson's a girl,'" she said. Used to "male-dominated environments" and "mickey taking" thanks to her dad's work as an engineer, she said she simply replied: "Yeah, Jackson's a girl." Now the Portsmouth-born presenter, also known for her reviews in print and on YouTube, says she has witnessed a surge in the number of women hitting the track. She said "loads of girls" had become interested in cars and she had even devised her own system for measuring the rise. "When I was a little girl going to the toilet at the motor racing circuits, there was no queue," Jackson told BBC Radio Solent. "And now you go to a motor racing circuit and the queue can be really long." After running her own used-car business, Jackson began racing at 26 and worked her way up from club level to compete at Le Mans, Dubai and the Nürburgring. Though men frequently outnumber women, Jackson said the racetrack itself acted as a leveller. "When you had your helmet on, nobody cared whether you were male or female, they just cared about beating the competition," she said. More stories from Hampshire & the Isle of Wight Watch the latest episode of South Today Listen to the latest news from Hampshire and the Isle of Wight Alongside her other work, Jackson has reviewed cars since 2011, and has presented on ITV4, Dave and Fifth Gear. In 2015, she and a co-driver set a Guinness World Record for the most countries visited by car on a single tank of fuel - covering 14 countries in an Audi A6. Now living in Berkshire with her seven-year-old twins, life remains in the fast lane. "I had this racing, writing media career that was... I didn't realise that all three things would be happening at once," she said. "Now instead of racing, I'm raising children. So my life has always been full. It's just full in a different way now." Despite juggling a media career and family, Jackson has managed to find some quieter moments. Jackson said her life continues to be busy after swapping the racetrack for raising twins [Getty Images] But those moments may not last long. Her son and daughter, both regulars at the skate park, have already revealed a passion for speed. "I'm a massive wheels person and so it's not a surprise, really, that my offspring will be interested in wheels," she said. "I've not forced this in any way." But Jackson said, ultimately, she wanted her children to do what made them happy. "I actually really like whatever they're interested in," she said. item.title: Where to watch Magic vs. Hawks today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener
item.description: Where to watch Magic vs. Hawks today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for NBA season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A new era in Orlando officially begins Wednesday as the Magic open Sean Sweeney's first season as a head coach against the Hawks . Orlando feels it has the pieces to compete after going up 3-1 on the East's top seed, the Pistons , in last year's playoffs. But that lead slipping away prompted the team to make a coaching change in hopes that a new voice will help the Magic move forward. The key will be keeping stars Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner healthy, which would allow Sweeney to maximize the potential of that pair alongside Desmond Bane. Fans will get their first look at the new setup in games that count Wednesday against the Hawks, who took two games off the Knicks in the opening round of the playoffs before New York lost just once more in the next three rounds on the way to the title. Jalen Johnson, CJ McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker are back to lead the way for Atlanta. It all kicks off Wednesday in Orlando. Here's all you need to know to tune in. Where to watch Magic vs. Hawks today TV channels: WRDQ-TV 27 (Orlando), ANF (Atlanta) Live streams: DAZN (Orlando), Fubo (Atlanta) The Magic vs. Hawks game will be televised locally by WRDQ-TV 27 in Orlando. Fans can also watch live and on-demand with DAZN in the Magic's broadcast territory. DAZN is Orlando's new direct-to-consumer media partner, set to air preseason and regular-season games along with additional Magic content all season long ( read more here ). All games not selected for exclusive national broadcast by one of the league's partners will be available to stream live and on-demand with DAZN, which offers a free trial for new subscribers. Fans in the Atlanta area can watch the game on ANF and stream it via Fubo . What time is Magic vs. Hawks today? Date: Wednesday, Oct. 21 Time: 7 p.m. ET The Magic vs. Hawks game is set to tip off Wednesday at 7 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Kia Center in Orlando, Florida. Magic schedule 2026-27 Here are Orlando's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 23 vs. Timberwolves 7 p.m. Oct. 25 at Knicks 7 p.m. Oct. 28 at Raptors 7:30 p.m. Oct. 30 at Raptors 7:30 p.m. Nov. 1 vs. Celtics 3:30 p.m. Hawks schedule 2026-27 Here are Atlanta's upcoming games: Date Game Time (ET) Oct. 23 at Hornets 7 p.m. Oct. 24 vs. Rockets 8:30 p.m. Oct. 26 at Rockets 8:30 p .m. Oct. 28 vs. Heat 7 p.m. Oct. 29 vs. Cavs 7 p.m. Related Links Latest NBA news and rumors Full NBA schedule, scores How to bet on the NBA The GOAT Debate: Michael Jordan vs. LeBron James

item.title: What time is Como vs. Man United? Live stream, TV channel, kickoff schedule for Champions League match
item.description: What time is Como vs. Man United? Live stream, TV channel, kickoff schedule for Champions League match originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Carrick has a massive chance to make a statement of intent as Manchester United travel to beautiful Lake Como for an early Champions League match on Wednesday. The Red Devils have had a rocky season so far, sitting 13th in the Premier League table with just one victory in seven domestic matches. They looked strong in their Champions League opener against Sabah at home, but then were humbled by Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano last week. Como, meanwhile, have been one of Italy's most fascinating stories the last two years, qualifying for the Champions League for the first time in club history this season and in the hunt again as they sit fifth in the Serie A table through seven matches. They won their opening Champions League game against RB Leipzig in flying fashion back in September, but fell to Dutch side Feyenoord last week. The Sporting News looks at the key details ahead of this game, including how to watch the match, kickoff times and the weekly schedule. Como vs. Man United start time This Champions League league phase clash takes place at Guiseppe Sinigaglia Stadium in Como, Italy and kicks off on Wednesday, October 21 at 6:45 p.m. local time. item.title: Fan Letters: Sunderland Need More From Granit Xhaka
item.description: BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: (EDITOR'S NOTE: Tonal effects have been applied to this image.) Granit Xhaka of Sunderland reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between AFC Bournemouth and Sunderland at Vitality Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) | Getty Images Want to have your say on all things Sunderland? Drop us a line and we’ll publish your views! RokerReport@yahoo.co.uk Dear Roker Report, For the second week running, Granit Xhaka has apologised to the fans for yet another woeful performance. We need action, Granit, not words. The body language of several players — including and especially our captain — is a major concern. When Xhaka joined the club last season, he said he wanted to experience something different; a challenge. Well, that’s exactly what you’ve got now, bonny lad. Be careful what you wish for! Fortunately, it’s October and not March, so hopefully things will improve. Buckle up, everyone. We might be in for a bumpy ride. Wayne Talbot Ed’s Note [Phil]: Hi, Wayne. Thank you for your letter. It’s been abundantly clear all season that Xhaka — the inspirational on-pitch figurehead and driving force behind last season’s European push — hasn’t hit the heights of 2025/2026 thus far, and naturally, theories are swirling as to why. Perhaps Chelsea is on his mind. He could still be suffering post-World Cup fatigue, or is there something else going on? Whatever it is, I fully agree that we need our captain to rally his men and begin to up his game if we’re to emerge from this worrying slump in league form and begin to climb the table. To that end, I wouldn’t dream of starting him against Lech Poznan tomorrow — he should see twenty minutes’ worth of action at the most. When he got on the microphone at the end of last season and made that memorable speech in which he gave us all cause for optimism ahead of 2026/2027, I doubt whether a season of struggle is what he had in mind. Let’s hope that he can rediscover his best form soon. Dear Roker Report, Although I’m not a supporter who attends away games now, I can’t believe the decision to make it compulsory for fans to use dedicated coaches to transport them to St James’ Park. Many fans live in the west side of County Durham. Others live near Teesside, and others north of the Tyne. Are these fans expected to travel to the Stadium of Light to use the official transport, or will the coaches travel around the outlying areas to various pick-up points? It seems ridiculous that those fans who live in those areas have to make a detour into Sunderland in order to get to Newcastle — particularly those who live north of the Tyne. Stuart Lathan Ed’s Note [Phil]: Hi, Stuart. Thank you for getting in touch. After last season’s pre-match trouble, during which amped-up Newcastle fans aimed missiles at the Sunderland team coach, it does seem somewhat overzealous to force our supporters to make their way to St James’ by official means only this t

item.title: Sunderland Have Issues, But They Are Fixable
item.description: Sunderland slipped into the relegation zone of the Premier League for the first time since the 2016/2017 season at the weekend, putting in a timid display in a match which had the hallmarks of an early season ‘six-pointer’. We travelled to a side without a win in the league yet this season — and my God, Bournemouth must’ve been delighted when, after less than twenty minutes, we’d shot ourselves in the foot. The issue is that it’s not the first time this season we’ve been our own worst enemy, but with games continuing to come thick and fast, we need to stop making it such a costly habit. Watching the game back, we looked sluggish and clumsy on the ball with no creativity outside or up top. Goals weren’t our strong point last season, but at least we had a solid defence which at times would rather die than let the ball get within striking distance of the goal. We’ve lost that this season other than on a couple of occasions, and now we look as weak as piss at the back and toothless up top. Some might say this is a recipe for disaster — and they’d be right. If we had £1 for every time one of our wingers had the ball and instead of going at the full back they turned around and played the ball back to a defender, we’d probably be able to go out and buy a winger that wouldn’t do this. I’ll caveat this and say this may be the attitude of wingers short on confidence, or it may be instruction from a head coach who often remains stubborn when it comes to changing the way we play. Whatever it is, it’s bloody frustrating and at times, it’s like watching paint dry. We’ve undoubtedly missed Brian Brobbey, but we simply can’t be reliant on one player to not just score goals but to make things happen for us. With Wilson Isidor or Timur Tutierov up top, we’ve looked like we have ten men and haven’t tried to play them into games. The defeats to Arsenal and Manchester City were promising, as they showed us battling for long periods. The Brighton match was a non-event on our part and the 2-0 loss down at Bournemouth was nothing short of pathetic. We can’t have more performances like that and hope to give ourselves a fighting chance of getting our season kickstarted. Rallying cries have been in short supply since full time on Sunday, but the words from Nordi Mukiele and Robin Roefs brought some comfort. This slump needs to be a wake-up call, and I don’t care if it’s naivety, complacency or something else — it’s not good enough for what we want to see in a Sunderland team. I’ll caveat this by saying we’ve had our injury issues, but I do this begrudgingly. Many teams in the league have players missing and do just fine. If there’s fragility within the squad, it needs rooting out now. After Lech Poznan, we have two huge games in which we should be going hell for leather in. Once on the other side of these matches and when November arrives, we’ll see if this was the case and if there’s still fight in this set of players.

item.title: 1 assist, 87% completed passes, 4 duels won: Jayce Fitzgerald shows growing maturity in Rotherham draw
item.description: 1 assist, 87% completed passes, 4 duels won: Jayce Fitzgerald shows growing maturity in Rotherham draw Manchester United had one player in loan action on Tuesday night. Playing situation Alongside Andre Onana, Jayce Fitzgerald has been the loanee who has received the most game time recently. Sekou Kone and Jacob Devaney are waiting for their suspensions to finish, and players like Dan Gore are still injured. Fitzgerald has often had to make do with a place on the bench for Rotherham United this season, but he got a start on Tuesday night. The Millers hosted Newport County and secured a 2-2 draw. The match The home side raced into the lead, scoring a penalty, and then Fitzgerald took over with a fine bit of midfield play. He won the ball back in the middle of the park and played an enticing through ball that split the Newport defence in half. Aaron Nemane made no mistake and fired into the bottom corner to give his side a 2-0 lead on the night. Fitzgerald had a key pass on the night and created one big chance as he grabbed his assist. He was also effective on the ball, completing an impressive 87% of his passes on the night. The young midfielder also had one shot that was blocked as he went in search of his first senior goal. He also completed one dribble, made a clearance, and one interception during the match. Fitzgerald was also competitive in the middle of the park, winning one tackle and a total of four duels in the match. The 19-year-old will be hoping for another start on Saturday afternoon when his side welcome Shrewsbury Town to the AESSEAL New York Stadium. item.title: Doué and Vitinha burn bright as brittle Barcelona come unstuck against PSG
item.description: Fire, noise, fury, a sense of empty energy. And across town, a football match too. Do any of these randomly pitched autumnal Champions League fixtures mean anything? Probably not when you’re Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, and the only game in town is risk-free TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stuff. But this was still a dazzling occasion at the Parc des Princes, where the champions of France and Spain played out a light, open, frictionless, exhibition-style game of football. PSG finished 4-2 winners, having been pegged back to 2-2 midway through the second half. But this was also a game where the score almost did not seem to matter, and where the only really hard message was the frailty of the Barcelona backline and PSG’s thrilling attacking energy in these midweek A-games. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: US under-17 women beat Samoa 17-0 for biggest win in World Cup history
item.description: Result is largest margin at any age level of a World Cup DiMaria is first to score six at Fifa finals since Haaland Tournament is in year two of expanded 24-team field The United States began their U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign on Monday with a record-setting 17-0 win over Samoa the biggest win at any age level in World Cup history. The result surpassed the previous record for margin at an 11-a-side World Cup, a 16-0 win by Morocco against New Caledonia in the 2025 U-17 men’s World Cup. Ten players scored for the US, and forward Maddie DiMaria led with six goals in Salé, Morocco. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country
item.description: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society The day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title. It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people. Continue reading...

item.title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
item.description: Peta calls on club to never again use a live animal mascot ‘There’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a stadium’ A leading animal rights group has urged Crystal Palace to retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk. In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’ academy; Charlie was on the fringes of their first team when the opportunity arose to join Toulouse in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play.” Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...
